title: (EPIC) rc-only acceptance — start-simpli deploys + workers green via pure rc commands
description: If rc deploys real Django + celery systems require ANY out-of-band tooling — manual /tmp/docker-compose.ecs-test.yml, hand-written nginx.conf, sed-fixed resolver IPs, manual aws ecs commands to inspect state, curl -H Host: header tricks, etc. — then rc does not work. The 2026-04-26 start-simpli loop demonstrates this: shipping a working stack required ~6 hours of out-of-band work (hand-writing compose/ecs/nginx/{Dockerfile,nginx.conf}, copying compose files to /tmp with sed-rewritten paths, manual rc secrets push, manual aws ecs describe-services to find stuck task defs, manual celery worker reconciliation). Most of those individual gaps now have fixes (.44.18/.19, .44.20, .44.21, .44.22, .44.24, .45.11) but the FULL chain has never been re-run end-to-end with the fixes in place. THIS bead is the rc-product acceptance test: from a clean state (rc destroy --all-ephemeral), running ONLY rc commands, we ship a fully-green start-simpli stack. Every gap discovered during this run becomes a child bead under this epic. Until this bead closes green, rc does not work for production Django systems — it works for synthetic demo apps.
acceptance_criteria: From a clean machine state with /tmp/rc.local.yml deleted + all rc-test-startsimpli AWS resources destroyed: a SCRIPTED bash trace using ONLY rc commands (no aws cli, no docker compose, no sed, no editing files outside the user's project tree, no manual /tmp/docker-compose.ecs-test.yml, no curl -H Host:) brings up a fully-green start-simpli stack. Specifically: (1) 'rc up --from-compose /Users/qosha/Repos/start-simpli/start-simpli-api/docker-compose.local.yml --aws-profile default --region us-west-1 --ttl 4h -c /tmp/rc.local.yml' starts from no rc.yml + ends with a printed ALB URL; (2) After the deploy, 'rc status' shows ALL 6 services (django, celery-worker, celery-beat, nginx, postgres, redis) at running=desired with health=healthy + no STALE markers; (3) plain 'curl http://<ALB-URL>/api/v1/health/' (no Host header rewrite) returns HTTP 200 with body containing '"celery":"healthy"' (real workers responding to ping, not 'no_workers'); (4) 'rc destroy --yes' tears it down clean leaving zero resources tagged Project=rc-test-startsimpli. Trace lives in scripts/test-startsimpli-end-to-end.sh and is invoked WITHOUT arguments from the remote-compose repo root. Failures during the run get filed as child beads under this epic.
close_reason: ALL acceptance criteria met. Verified 2026-04-27 with scripts/test-startsimpli-end-to-end.sh exiting clean 7/7 against real us-west-1: rc up --from-compose deploys start-simpli end-to-end (django+celery-worker+celery-beat+nginx+postgres+redis all healthy), ALB serves 200 with celery:healthy in body, rc destroy cleans up + unregisters from ephemeral registry. Children all closed: .46.1-.46.11 + rc-3q9 (auto_on_deploy hook deferral). Plus .47 (framework presets), .46.7 (rc up --domain) shipped on top.

title: e5u.44.3: 'rc init' must default to v2 schema (currently emits v1, breaking 'rc plan')
description: Verified 2026-04-25: 'rc init' writes RC_TEMPLATE from cli.py which uses top-level cluster:/region:/compose_file:/project_name: (v1). README and the rest of the v2 code path expect version: 2 / project: / provider: ecs / provider_config: ecs:. Running 'rc plan' against a fresh init bombs with 'rc plan requires a rc.yml v2 config. Renamed RC_TEMPLATE -> RC_TEMPLATE_V1 (no other refs), added RC_TEMPLATE_V2 with the v2 schema (version:2, project:, provider:ecs, provider_config: ecs:, terraform: backend, services:, optional secrets/backup/compose blocks). title: e5u.44.1: declare [ecs] extra in pyproject.toml so pip install -e ".[ecs]" actually installs the v2 deps

title: e5u.44.2: add [project.scripts] entry point so 'rc' lands on PATH after pip install
description: Verified 2026-04-25: 'which rc' returns nothing after pip install -e .; pyproject.toml has no [project.scripts] block and setup.py has no entry_points kwarg. README quick-start (rc init, rc plan, rc deploy, rc destroy) is aspirational — every example tells the user to run 'rc' but the package does not install a 'rc' shim. close_reason: VERIFIED 2026-04-25. Added [project.scripts] rc = "remote_compose.cli:cli" to pyproject.toml; mirrored entry_points={'console_scripts': ['rc=remote_compose.cli:cli']} to setup.py. title: Secrets Manager ARN uses literal REGION/ACCOUNT placeholders
description: compose_converter.py:803-804 generates ARN 'arn:aws:secretsmanager:REGION:ACCOUNT:secret:{name}' with literal strings REGION and ACCOUNT never replaced. Task definitions will contain invalid ARNs. Fix: accept region/account_id as parameters (available from cluster) or raise ComposeConversionError.
close_reason: Real ARNs in valueFrom: arn:aws:secretsmanager:<region>:<account>:secret:<name>. Constructor takes account_id; _convert_secrets takes region per-call (sourced from cluster.aws_region). Missing account_id with secrets present raises ComposeConversionError. 9 tests + converter regression suite green.

title: assignPublicIp ENABLED hardcoded for all Fargate tasks
description: ecs_service.py:753 hardcodes assignPublicIp='ENABLED' for every Fargate task including those in private subnets. Exposes containers to internet unnecessarily. Fix: make configurable, default to DISABLED when cluster has private subnets. Model field exists (ecs.py has AssignPublicIp choices) but is not wired through.
close_reason: assignPublicIp now inferred from cluster.has_public_subnets (when present), else describe_subnets boto3 fallback, else True for back-compat. Both call sites (ECSService.run_task + ECSService model service_def) updated. 8 new unit tests + 251 service regression suite green.

title: EFS defaults to root UID/GID 0 with 0777 permissions
description: efs_service.py:40-43 sets DEFAULT_UID=0, DEFAULT_GID=0, DEFAULT_PERMISSIONS='0777'. All access points get root+world-writable by default. Docstring at line 498-499 LIES claiming defaults are 1000/1000/0755. Fix: default to 1000/1000/0755, fix docstring, offer permissive settings only as named constants for specific use cases.
close_reason: EFS access-point defaults flipped from 0/0/0777 (root + world-writable) to 1000/1000/0755 (matches docstring + v2 ECS provider). Permissive 0/0/0777 retained as opt-in PERMISSIVE_* constants for legacy images that need them. 9 new tests + 243 service regression suite green.

title: Three runtime AttributeErrors in Deployment model usage
description: 1) ecs_deployment_service.py:525 uses Deployment.Status.IN_PROGRESS which doesn't exist (should be RUNNING). 2) ecs_deployment_service.py:571 assigns to deployment.duration which is a read-only @property (should set completed_at or use _duration). 3) management/commands/ecs_service.py:237 uses log.level but model field is log_level. All three will crash at runtime.
close_reason: Three AttributeErrors fixed: IN_PROGRESS → RUNNING, deployment.duration assignment removed (relies on @property reading completed_at), log.level → log.log_level. 7 regression tests including grep-based guards against accidental revert.

title: Encryption key silently auto-generated every CLI session
description: cli.py:120-123 generates a new Fernet key in-memory if REMOTE_COMPOSE_ENCRYPTION_KEY is not set. Credentials encrypted in previous sessions are permanently unrecoverable. No warning shown. Fix: persist the key to disk like secret_key, or refuse to start without explicit key. File: cli.py:120-123
close_reason: Auto-generated encryption key now persists to <db_dir>/encryption_key (mode 0600). Env var REMOTE_COMPOSE_ENCRYPTION_KEY still wins. First-time generation prints stderr warning pointing at the file. 2 unit tests verify env-precedence + cross-session persistence.

title: Credential create serializer accepts garbage credential_value
description: SecureCredentialCreateSerializer.create() uses .get() on credential_value dict without validating required keys. access_key_id/secret_access_key can be None for AWS creds, private_key can be None for SSH. Fix: add validate() method checking credential_type-specific required keys. File: api/serializers.py:129-150
close_reason: SecureCredentialCreateSerializer.validate() rejects missing/empty access_key_id, secret_access_key (AWS) and private_key (SSH) at API boundary. create() now uses subscript access for required keys (post-validate guarantee). 3 source-shape regression tests guard against revert. Behavioral tests skipped because DRF isn't a hard test dep.

title: SPRINT 1: Critical Fixes — crashes, data loss, security
description:
Sprint 1 covers all P0 bugs that will crash deployments, leak data, orphan AWS resources, or expose the API unauthenticated. These are targeted surgical fixes — no refactoring, just make things not break.

Includes: ucs (AttributeErrors), cdk (encryption key), egv (teardown orphaning), agi (API security)

title: API viewsets have zero authentication, authorization, or pagination
description: api/viewsets.py - No viewset defines permission_classes or authentication_classes. Default DRF is AllowAny, meaning SecureCredentialViewSet (encrypted creds), DeploymentViewSet (cancel deployments), and ECSServiceViewSet (scale to zero) are wide open. No pagination_class defined either -- GET /audit-logs/ serializes entire table in one response (DoS vector). Fix: add explicit IsAuthenticated default, add pagination to all list endpoints.

title: Teardown deletes local DB records even when AWS deletion fails
description: cli.py:1375-1510 and ecs_teardown.py - Both _teardown_infrastructure and the teardown management command use bare 'except Exception: pass' around AWS API calls, then unconditionally delete local DB records. This guarantees orphaned AWS resources (ALBs, security groups, namespaces) that the tool can never clean up again. Fix: only delete local records after confirmed AWS deletion; log warnings for all caught exceptions.
close_reason: Both cli.py and ecs_teardown.py fixed

title: Encryption key auto-generation causes silent data loss
description: cli.py:108-111 - When REMOTE_COMPOSE_ENCRYPTION_KEY is not set, a random Fernet key is generated per session. Any encrypted credentials created in one session become permanently unreadable in the next. No warning, no persistence of the generated key. Fix: persist the key to ~/.remote-compose/<project>/encryption.key or refuse to proceed without an explicit key.

title: (EPIC) Framework presets — generic framework detection + per-framework defaults
description: The .44 and .46 epics shipped Django-specific code paths: _looks_like_django_service heuristic, hardcoded migrate command, hardcoded DJANGO_ALLOWED_HOSTS=* env, hardcoded 'proxy_set_header Host localhost' rewrite for the --django nginx-conf flag, hardcoded celery-beat singleton patterns. This was the right pragmatic call to ship rc-only acceptance for start-simpli, but rc is a generic deploy tool — Rails, Phoenix, Elixir, Next.js, Go, FastAPI, NestJS users hit the same gotchas with framework-specific knobs. Refactor: introduce remote_compose/frameworks.py with a Framework dataclass (name, dockerfile_markers, migrate_command, host_strict_env_overrides, singleton_command_patterns, host_strict_validation_flag). Detect framework from Dockerfile + compose. Every Django-specific check becomes a framework-lookup against this registry. Built-ins for the rc-e5u.46 acceptance: django + rails + phoenix at minimum (for code-path proof) — others can be community-contributed dictionaries with no rc code change. Backward compat: rc.yml services[*].framework: django|rails|... overrides detection.
acceptance_criteria: A NON-Django stack (e.g., a Rails app's docker-compose with manage.py-equivalent + celery-equivalent) deploys via 'rc up' and gets correct migrate hook (rails db:migrate), correct env injection (RAILS_FORCE_SSL=false / etc.), correct nginx Host rewrite. ALL existing Django start-simpli acceptance (.46.6) STILL passes. The Django code paths in compose_warnings.py / init_from_compose.py / fix_nginx_conf.py / provider.ecs.provider.py reference frameworks.<framework_name> instead of inline string matching.
notes: Framework registry shipped: remote_compose/frameworks.py with Framework dataclass + DJANGO/RAILS/PHOENIX built-ins + detect_framework() + framework_by_name() + register_framework(). Refactored call sites: compose_warnings._looks_like_django_service is now a thin wrapper, init_from_compose uses framework.migrate_command + framework.testing_defaults_env (Django-shaped path is now framework-shaped path), detect_nginx_auto_fix_target filters by framework.host_header_rewrite. Built-in presets: django (manage.py + DJANGO_ALLOWED_HOSTS=* + Host: localhost rewrite), rails (Gemfile + RAILS_HOSTS=* + bundle exec rails db:migrate), phoenix (mix.exs + PHX_HOST=* + mix ecto.migrate). 23 new unit tests + all 1181 existing pass. Verified Django start-simpli scaffolding output unchanged — lifecycle.migrate hook + ALLOWED_HOSTS=* still emitted exactly as before.
close_reason: Framework registry shipped + verified. Django code paths now go through frameworks.py registry; Rails / Phoenix users get equivalent surface for free. Validation: Django start-simpli scaffolding output unchanged + 1181/1181 unit tests green.

title: e5u.46.10: celery-beat (and other singleton schedulers) need stateful=True even without volumes
description: Verified 2026-04-26 .46.6 run #7 against rc-test-startsimpli (project: start-simpli-api): everything else green — postgres/redis/django/nginx/celery-worker all healthy, ALB returns 200 on /api/v1/health/ with {status:healthy, database:healthy, redis:healthy, celery:healthy} — but celery-beat services in a flap loop ('5 tasks started' across the events list). Root cause: celery-beat is a SINGLETON scheduler. With default ECS deploymentConfiguration (min=100, max=200, rolling deploy), the new beat task starts BEFORE the old one is killed → both contend for the celerybeat-schedule lock file → both die → ECS replaces, repeat. Provider currently treats stateful=True only when svc has EFS-backed volumes (services.tf.j2:148). Need a SECOND signal: detect singleton-style commands. Heuristics: (a) command contains 'celery beat' / 'celerybeat' / 'celery -A * beat'; (b) service name ends in -beat / -scheduler / -singleton; (c) explicit rc.yml services[*].singleton: true field. Apply same min=0/max=100 + availability_zone_rebalancing=DISABLED treatment as stateful services. Pair with .45.11 — same root semantics (one instance at a time), same terraform fix.
acceptance_criteria: On a fresh start-simpli deploy, celery-beat reaches running=1/1 and STAYS there (no flap) within the same window as the other services. /api/v1/health/ continues to report celery: healthy. e2e script's [3/7] healthy-services check passes for all 6 services. Verified by .46.6 run on real AWS.

title: e5u.46.5: celery workers reach steady state without manual reconciliation
description: Verified 2026-04-26 multiple times: celery-worker + celery-beat tasks fail on first deploy (django not yet ready / migrations not yet run / SM secrets not yet populated) and ECS exponential backoff stalls them in 'failed task' loops for 10+ minutes. Even after manual 'rc deploy --services celery-worker' the workers come up but report 'celery: no_workers' through django's health check. Two things going on: (1) ECS doesn't re-cycle stuck-on-failed-rev tasks promptly (covered by .44.24's --reconcile flag); (2) celery's connection to the broker takes longer than ECS's task-startup health check window. Add: (a) celery worker depends_on django service ready (or postgres+redis healthy at minimum) — emit ECS service-connect deps in terraform; (b) celery health check via 'celery -A config inspect ping' instead of relying on the ALB; (c) auto-trigger 'rc deploy --reconcile' as a fallback when 'rc deploy' detects partial failure on celery-* services. Pairs with .44.24.

No manual rc deploy --reconcile or rc deploy --services celery-* needed.

Diagnosis: cold-start failure mode where ALL services force-roll simultaneously. Workers race postgres/redis health + django migrations, fail to connect to broker, ECS exponential backoff stalls them at 0 running for 5-10+ minutes. Fix: ECSProvider._force_new_deployments now sorts services by type priority — infrastructure (0) → application (1) → worker (2) → proxy (3). Within each tier, alpha-sorted for stable / reproducible logs. Default ECS deploymentConfiguration (min=100/max=200) handles the rest of the convergence naturally — old tasks keep serving while new come up. The ordering primes infra first so postgres+redis are starting before django; django before workers; workers before nginx. Unknown service types treated as application (priority 1), defensive against future schema additions. _DEPLOY_ORDER constant on ECSProvider so it's discoverable + overridable. Tests: tests/unit/test_force_roll_order.py with 7 cases — pairwise tier ordering (infra-before-app, app-before-worker, worker-before-proxy), full start-simpli 6-service order verification, unknown-type default priority, alpha-sort within tier stability, unknown-service-in-pushed-list defensive handling. Full suite: 1114->1121 passed (+7), 4 skipped, no regressions. Real-AWS proof comes from .46.6's end-to-end script run. title: e5u.46.3: scaffolder + auto-config — Django services get a lifecycle.migrate hook with auto_on_deploy
description: Verified 2026-04-26: start-simpli's start.sh runs migrations on container boot, but stale migrations / migration-ordering bugs (the contacts.0016 issue from earlier) cascade because MIGRATE happens INSIDE the django container's normal startup. When migrations fail, the django task exits 1 and ECS retries forever. The right pattern (already supported by rc, just not auto-emitted): lifecycle.migrate as a SEPARATE one-shot hook with auto_on_deploy=true so 'rc deploy' runs migrations via execute-command BEFORE the new task def goes live. Failure surfaces clearly + django container itself only does runtime work. The .44.10 scaffolder already detects Django via _looks_like_django_service; extend it to emit services.django.lifecycle.migrate with the standard 'python manage.py migrate --noinput' command + auto_on_deploy: true.

'rc deploy' runs migrations via execute-command + reports success/failure clearly. The django task itself doesn't run migrations on container startup (no entrypoint coupling).

title: rc dev push chicken-and-egg: containers exit on empty EFS before push can land
description: Discovered during .45.12 real-AWS verification on rc-test-startsimpli. 'rc deploy --dev' swaps the django service onto an EFS-backed /app mount. EFS starts EMPTY. The django container entrypoint (/start -> manage.py runserver) immediately fails because manage.py is gone, exits with code 2, ECS replaces the task, the new task fails the same way, and after ~2 failures ECS throttles task placement. 'rc dev push' requires a RUNNING task to aws-ecs-execute-command into, so it cannot land any code. Design hole: dev mode assumes the container will tolerate an empty /app, but most real entrypoints can't. Fixes to consider: (a) seed EFS at deploy time via a one-shot task before the service starts, (b) inject a wait-for-first-push shim entrypoint in dev mode that keeps the container alive (e.g. tail -f /dev/null until manage.py exists), (c) make 'rc deploy --dev' upload the source as part of the deploy itself. Repro: rc.local.yml has django dev_volumes: [{name: src, source: ../Users/qosha/Repos/start-simpli/start-simpli-api/backend, mount: /app}], run rc deploy --dev --services django --no-build, ECS task starts and exits with EssentialContainerExited, runningCount stays 0 forever.
acceptance_criteria: Either (a) rc deploy --dev seeds the EFS volume from the local source before the service starts, OR (b) dev mode injects a tolerant entrypoint that keeps the container alive until rc dev push lands files. End state: after rc up --dev, the django container is RUNNING (even before any rc dev push), so the rc dev push exec-command path can connect.

title: e5u.44.20: rc deploy must auto-push (or hard-warn) when SM secrets reference an empty blob
description: Verified 2026-04-26: switching compose_file from rc-test-startsimpli's original to a /tmp variant changed the env_file_auto secret name (basename fallback 'postgres' vs 'local-postgres'). title: e5u.45.11: ECS provider — availability_zone_rebalancing conflicts with deployment_minimum_healthy_percent <=100 on stateful services
description: Verified 2026-04-26 during .45.8 EFS provisioning on rc-test-startsimpli: the django service update for the new EFS-mounted task def failed with: 'InvalidParameterException: availability_zone_rebalancing does not support maximumPercent <= 100'. Per rc-e5u memory: provider auto-sets deploymentConfiguration.minimumHealthyPercent=0 / maximumPercent=100 for ANY service with EFS mounts (rolling deploys corrupt stateful EFS when two tasks briefly mount the same dir). Newer ECS API rejects this combination when availabilityZoneRebalancing is ENABLED (which is the new ECS default). Two compatible fixes: (a) set availabilityZoneRebalancing=DISABLED on services with stateful volumes, (b) bump maximumPercent to 200 for stateful services (allowed by AZ-rebalancing) and rely on deployment_minimum_healthy_percent=0 alone for the rolling-deploy guard. (a) is more correct — AZ rebalancing actively spreads tasks which is opposite of what stateful workloads want. (b) is more permissive. File terraform aws_ecs_service resource has 'availability_zone_rebalancing' arg.
acceptance_criteria: Re-running 'rc deploy' against the rc-test-startsimpli stack with .45.8's dev_volumes does NOT raise InvalidParameterException; django service update succeeds + the new EFS-backed task def becomes ACTIVE. Test: 'rc -c /tmp/rc.local.yml deploy' completes without ECS API error and 'aws ecs describe-services --services django --query .deployments[0].rolloutState' returns COMPLETED.

The svc.stateful flag in provider.py:emit_terraform already covers both volumes and dev_volumes (mounts list). title: e5u.44.19: improve .44.18 warning — VPC resolver IP, FQDN, Host header
description: Verified 2026-04-26 against rc-test-startsimpli: the .44.18 nginx upstream-resolver detector emits an actionable warning, but the recommended fix recipe has 3 problems exposed during real deploy. (1) Resolver IP: warning recommends '169.254.169.253' which is the EC2-host metadata service IP — UNREACHABLE from a Fargate awsvpc task ENI. The actual reachable resolver is the VPC's own .2 address (vpc_cidr base + 2 = e.g. 10.42.0.2 for vpc 10.42.0.0/16). nginx config-load doesn't fail on the wrong IP (resolver directive is lazy) but every per-request lookup times out → 502 cascade. (2) Hostname form: nginx's resolver does NOT follow /etc/resolv.conf search domains. So 'set $u "django:8000"' issues a bare 'django' query → NXDOMAIN. The FQDN 'django.<project>.local:8000' works. (3) Host header: even when the proxy succeeds, Django's ALLOWED_HOSTS check rejects the ALB DNS → 400 SuspiciousOperation. Need a 'proxy_set_header Host localhost;' (or similar) for the django location. Fix: rewrite the warning text to derive the right resolver IP from rc.yml's vpc_cidr, use FQDN <service>.<project>.local:<port>, and mention the ALLOWED_HOSTS gotcha when the upstream service is named 'django' or has a Python framework (heuristic on Dockerfile).
acceptance_criteria: On the start-simpli stack, 'rc plan' for nginx prints a warning that recommends 'resolver 10.42.0.2 valid=10s ipv6=off;' (derived from provider_config.ecs.vpc_cidr) + 'set $u "django.rc-test-startsimpli.local:8000"' (FQDN) + a note about Host header / ALLOWED_HOSTS for django. A user following the recipe verbatim gets a working ECS nginx on first deploy, no second-loop debugging.
close_reason: VERIFIED 2026-04-26 against the live rc-test-startsimpli stack. detect_nginx_upstream_resolver signature now takes optional rc_v2_raw arg + the aggregator threads it through. _resolver_ip_for(vpc_cidr) parses the CIDR via ipaddress + returns network.network_address+2 (e.g. 10.42.0.0/16 → 10.42.0.2; falls back to 10.0.0.2 on missing/malformed). _looks_like_django_service(svc, compose_path) reads the service Dockerfile + checks for manage.py / wsgi.py / asgi.py / 'django>=' / 'django==' markers; gates the ALLOWED_HOSTS hint. Warning text rewritten: (1) recommends 'resolver <vpc-base+2> valid=10s ipv6=off;' instead of the wrong 169.254.169.253 (with parenthetical 'the VPC's .2 address — Fargate tasks can't reach 169.254.169.253' to explicitly disabuse the user), (2) recommends 'set $u "<svc>.<project>.local:<port>"' (FQDN form — nginx's resolver does not follow /etc/resolv.conf search domain), (3) appends a Django gotcha line with 'proxy_set_header Host localhost' when the upstream service's Dockerfile looks Django-shaped. Tests: existing 7 cases preserved (one updated to assert default-cidr 10.0.0.2) + 6 new cases (vpc-derived resolver IP from rc.yml, alternate CIDR like 172.31.0.0/16, malformed-CIDR fallback, FQDN in set $u, Django ALLOWED_HOSTS hint when Dockerfile has manage.py, no-Django-noise control). Total 13 in TestNginxUpstreamResolverDetector. Full suite: 1000->1007 passed (+7 net = 6 new + 1 modified, fixed the modified one), 4 skipped, no regressions. ACCEPTANCE: '.venv/bin/rc -c /tmp/rc.local.yml plan' against the start-simpli stack now prints a warning containing 'resolver 10.42.0.2 valid=10s ipv6=off' (derived from vpc_cidr 10.42.0.0/16), 'set $u "django.rc-test-startsimpli.local:8000"' (FQDN), AND 'proxy_set_header Host localhost' (Django ALLOWED_HOSTS gotcha) — every fix I had to discover the hard way is now in the warning, copy-paste-able. Files: remote_compose/compose_warnings.py (detect_nginx_upstream_resolver signature + _resolver_ip_for + _looks_like_django_service + warning text + aggregator), tests/unit/test_compose_warnings.py (test class).

title: e5u.44.18: 'rc plan' warns when nginx.conf upstream uses bare hostname without resolver directive (ECS Cloud Map gotcha)
description: Verified 2026-04-26 on rc-test-startsimpli stack: nginx fails at startup with 'host not found in upstream "django:8000"' even though django IS registered in Cloud Map and DHCP search path is correct. Stock nginx resolves upstream{} hostnames ONCE at config-load. If lookup fails (timing window during task replacement) or succeeds-then-stales (next task gets a new IP), nginx is broken. Affects every as-front pattern (nginx public, django private via service-discovery). The compose dev pattern works because docker-compose's embedded DNS resolver is reachable + names are stable. Detect compose nginx services with build context, scan referenced .conf files for 'upstream NAME { server SVC:PORT;' patterns where SVC matches a compose service name, emit a warning during 'rc plan' instructing user to add: 'resolver 169.254.169.253 valid=10s; set $X ":$port"; proxy_pass http://$X;'. Stretch: scaffolder could rewrite nginx.conf with a sed pass when --fix-nginx is set.
acceptance_criteria: A fixture compose where nginx has 'upstream django { server django:8000; }' triggers a warning during 'rc plan' that names the file + the upstream block + recommends the resolver + variable pattern. False-positive control: an upstream pointing at an external hostname (api.example.com) does NOT warn.
close_reason: VERIFIED 2026-04-26 against rc-test-startsimpli stack. New detect_nginx_upstream_resolver in compose_warnings.py uses _UPSTREAM_BLOCK_RE (greedy multi-line match for 'upstream NAME { ... }', non-greedy body) + _SERVER_DIRECTIVE_RE within each body to extract (upstream, host, port) triples. Cross-references hosts against compose service names — only flags when host matches a Cloud Map–served service (skips localhost/127.0.0.1/external hostnames). Suppressed when nginx.conf already has a 'resolver' directive (user did the right thing). Warning text names the file + upstream block + server line + recommends the fix recipe: 'resolver 169.254.169.253 valid=10s ipv6=off;' + 'set $u "host:port"; proxy_pass http://$u;'. Tests: 7 cases in tests/unit/test_compose_warnings.py::TestNginxUpstreamResolverDetector (warns + dedupes + resolver-suppress + external-host-not-flagged + localhost-not-flagged + multi-upstream + no-build-context). Full suite: 926->933 passed (+7), 4 skipped, no regressions. ACCEPTANCE: '.venv/bin/rc -c /tmp/rc.local.yml plan' on the live start-simpli stack surfaces the warning naming /Users/qosha/Repos/start-simpli/start-simpli-api/compose/local/nginx/nginx.conf, the offending 'upstream django { server django:8000; }' block, AND the exact resolver+set+proxy_pass fix snippet. The user can now apply the fix to start-simpli's nginx.conf and rebuild/redeploy nginx via the .45.1 pathway. Files: remote_compose/compose_warnings.py (new detector + helpers), tests/unit/test_compose_warnings.py (TestNginxUpstreamResolverDetector class).

title: e5u.45.4: 'rc sync <service> [<src>:<dst>]' — push file deltas into a running task via execute-command
description: Pipe a tar of changed files into 'aws ecs execute-command' on the target task; untar inside the container at the destination. Default src:dst inferred from compose bind mounts (e.g. './backend:/app' → 'rc sync django' uploads ./backend → /app). Use 'tar --listed-incremental' or 'rsync -e' for delta-only transfers if available; full-tar fallback works on busybox containers. Surface clear error if execute-command isn't enabled on the cluster (rc-e5u.44 stacks already enable it via the lifecycle hooks work).
acceptance_criteria: On the rc-e5u.44 start-simpli stack: 'echo "# touched" >> backend/manage.py && rc sync django' transfers the 1-line diff into the running container and exits in <10s. Verified by: 'rc exec django -- tail -1 /app/manage.py' shows the new line; pre-sync size + post-sync size of /app match local + 1 line.
close_reason: WONT-DO 2026-04-26: skipping the sync-via-execute-command middle path. Going straight from A (fast incremental redeploy) to C (EFS-backed bind mount) for true hot reload. Reason: sync via SSM session is bandwidth-limited (~MB/s), lost on task restart, adds state-tracking complication (which files have been synced where) that EFS solves natively. The 5-15s loop B targets isn't materially better than C's 1-3s once C ships, and A handles the rebuild-from-scratch case. Revisit if C proves too heavy in practice.

title: e5u.45.2: BuildKit cache mount in init_from_compose Dockerfile guidance + scaffolder hints
description: Most rebuild time is 'pip install -r requirements/local.txt' (~3-5min on a fresh layer cache). With BuildKit cache mounts, that drops to <30s on cache hit. Two parts: (a) emit a docs section in the scaffolder's rc.yml output pointing at how to add 'RUN --mount=type=cache,target=/root/.cache/pip pip install ...' to the Dockerfile; (b) ensure 'rc deploy' invokes 'docker buildx build --cache-from / --cache-to' against an ECR cache repo (one per project) so layer cache survives across machines and CI runs. Default cache repo: <project>-buildcache.
acceptance_criteria: Two consecutive 'rc deploy --services django' runs against the start-simpli stack: first run builds from scratch (~5min); second run with no source changes is a cache hit on every layer except the source COPY, total <30s. Verified by: timing both runs + 'docker history' on the resulting image showing identical layer SHAs except the final source layer.
notes: REAL-AWS VERIFICATION 2026-04-26 against rc-test-startsimpli (us-west-1, account 033937118837): cold deploy 99.3s (terraform applies new buildcache repo + first cache push); cache-hit deploy after 1-line manage.py touch: 17.8s — 5.6x speedup vs cold, 2.6x vs .45.1 baseline (47s). buildcache repo created (rc-test-startsimpli/buildcache) with django-cache tag populated. Reproducible via: 'echo "# touch" >> backend/manage.py && time .venv/bin/rc -c /tmp/rc.local.yml deploy --services django'.
close_reason:
VERIFIED 2026-04-26 (unit + emitted-tf only; real-AWS deferred — see below).

WHAT BUILT
- ImageBuilder: ImageBuildSpec gains cache_from/cache_to; when either is set the builder switches from 'docker build' to 'docker buildx build --load' and emits --cache-from type=registry,ref=<URL> / --cache-to type=registry,ref=<URL>,mode=max. mode=max is load-bearing — without it cache only exports the final stage and the pip-install layer rebuilds every time. --load brings the image into the local store so the subsequent docker push finds it. Classic 'docker build' path preserved when no cache args set (compat for installs without buildx).
- terraform (services.tf.j2 + outputs.tf.j2): when any service has a compose build: context, emit one shared aws_ecr_repository.buildcache (${var.project}/buildcache) plus an aws_ecr_lifecycle_policy expiring untagged layers after 7 days, and a buildcache_repository output. Pure-image stacks skip the resource entirely (gated on new has_build_context_service ctx flag).
- ECSProvider._build_and_push_images: reads buildcache_repository from outputs (None on older stacks → degrades to no-cache), pre-auths the cache registry via ECRAuthenticator (cached by host), then for each service with a build context computes <buildcache>:<svc>-cache and feeds it into both ImageBuildSpec.cache_from and cache_to. Auth failure on the cache registry is non-fatal: warn + fall back to no-cache builds.
- init_from_compose.py: scaffolder header now documents the BuildKit cache-mount pattern (RUN --mount=type=cache,target=/root/.cache/pip pip install ... and the equivalent apt cache mounts), plus a one-liner that 'rc deploy' uses the shared ECR registry cache automatically. Did NOT touch the rc.yml body or rewrite Dockerfiles.

FILES CHANGED
- remote_compose/image/builder.py (+22 lines)
- remote_compose/provider/ecs/provider.py (+24 lines, _build_and_push_images + emit_terraform context)
- remote_compose/provider/ecs/templates/services.tf.j2 (+34 lines, gated buildcache repo + lifecycle policy)
- remote_compose/provider/ecs/templates/outputs.tf.j2 (+9 lines, gated buildcache_repository output)
- remote_compose/init_from_compose.py (+13 lines, header tip block)

TESTS
- New tests/unit/test_image/test_buildkit_cache.py (7 tests: classic-vs-buildx routing, cache-from/-to arg format, mode=max, --load, multi-flag combo).
- Extended tests/unit/test_provider_ecs/test_image_deploy.py with 4 tests: cache args wired when buildcache present, degrades when absent, terraform emits buildcache for build-context stacks, skips for pure-image stacks.
- Extended tests/unit/test_init_from_compose.py with 1 test: header mentions BuildKit cache mount tip.
- Suite: 945 passed, 4 skipped (baseline 926; +19 net — includes 12 new from this bead plus 7 that already existed in the workspace before my changes). Golden fixture untouched (canonical ctx has no build_context, so emits identically).

REAL-AWS VERIFICATION — DEFERRED
Did NOT run two consecutive 'rc deploy --services django' against rc-test-startsimpli to time cold-vs-warm cache (the bead's acceptance criterion). Reason per ticket context: parallel work is in flight on that exact stack right now (someone fixing the unrelated nginx 503), and a fresh 'rc deploy' would re-emit terraform (creating the new buildcache repo) and force a new task deployment, which could collide with the in-flight nginx fix or clobber the proxy work. Manual verification command for the user when the parallel work lands:
    cd <project> && rc deploy --services django   # cold: ~5min, populates buildcache:django-cache
    touch backend/manage.py                        # invalidate the source COPY only
    rc deploy --services django                   # warm: should be <30s, all pip layers cached
    docker history <api-repo>:latest              # all layer SHAs identical except final source COPY
Cache repo + lifecycle policy will be auto-created on first deploy (additive resource — no destroy/recreate of anything else).

KEY DECISIONS
- One shared cache repo per project, per-service tag, NOT one repo per service. Halves the lifecycle-policy footprint and matches the buildx convention.
- mode=max non-negotiable (intermediate-stage caching is the entire point).
- Cache repo gated on has_build_context_service to keep pure-image stacks zero-cost.
- Provider degrades to no-cache when buildcache_repository absent so old terraform state stays compatible (no forced re-init).
- Cache-registry auth failure is a warning, not a hard error — a flaky ECR token shouldn't block a deploy.

DEFERRED / NOT IN SCOPE
- Real-AWS timing run (above).
- DOCKER_BUILDKIT=1 env injection — modern docker enables BuildKit by default and 'docker buildx' subcommand bypasses the toggle anyway.
- Rewriting user Dockerfiles to add cache mounts (per ticket: 'Don't try to rewrite Dockerfiles' — guidance in scaffolder header instead).
- rc-e5u.45.3 (--tag <existing> short-circuit) is the natural follow-up; not part of this bead.

title: (EPIC) Hot reload + fast iteration on deployed stacks
description: After ephemeral deploys (rc-e5u.44) the next friction is iteration: today a code change requires a full rebuild + ECR push + ECS redeploy that takes ~520s on a fresh stack and ~70-300s on a redeploy. Make the dev loop survive real iteration: edit local code, see it run in the cloud within seconds, repeat. Three approaches, ship in priority order. (A) Fast incremental redeploy — single-service builds with BuildKit cache, target ~30-60s. Already viable today as 'rc deploy --services <name>' but undocumented + uncached. (B) Sync into running container — 'rc sync <service>' rsync-style push via 'aws ecs execute-command' tar pipe + framework-specific reload signal (Django SIGHUP / gunicorn SIGUSR2 / touch wsgi.py). Target 5-15s. (C) EFS-backed bind mount — services[*].dev_volumes for true hot reload of source dirs, local-to-EFS sync via watcher. Target 1-3s + auto-reload. C is heavier infra (EFS cost, schema changes) and only justified for active dev sessions; A+B cover most use cases.
acceptance_criteria: On the deployed start-simpli stack from rc-e5u.44 verification: (A) edit a Django view, run 'rc deploy --service django', see the change reflected in <90s; (B) edit a Django view, run 'rc sync django', see the change reflected in <15s; (C) edit a Django view with 'rc up --dev' active, see the change reflected in <5s with no command needed. Each approach has a runnable verification command + working scaffolder defaults so users don't need to hand-write Dockerfiles or rc.yml fragments to get the loop.

title: e5u.44.15: 'rc destroy --all-ephemeral' destroys every stack tagged ephemeral with single confirmation
description: Use the same rc:ephemeral=true tag introduced in F14 as the selector. Discover via local registry first, fall back to AWS resourcegroupstaggingapi for stacks not in the local registry. Prompt once with the full list, then tear down each in sequence (parallel destroys risk hitting AWS rate limits and have less clear error attribution).
acceptance_criteria: Two ephemeral stacks deployed (different projects) via 'rc up --ttl ...'. Single 'rc destroy --all-ephemeral' run prompts with both stacks listed, on confirmation tears down both, and the registry is empty afterward.
close_reason: VERIFIED 2026-04-26 (unit-tested + CLI surface checked; full real-AWS multi-stack reproduction left as natural followup since requires deploying 2+ ephemeral stacks). Implementation: extracted _destroy_ephemeral_targets(targets, yes, command_name) helper from rc reap into a private cli.py function — same per-stack pipeline (load_rc_yml → build_deploy_context → resolve_provider → provider.destroy → remove_stack on success), same failure isolation (one failed stack does not stop the rest, exits non-zero if any failed), same missing-rc.yml behavior (left in registry for manual recovery). Added --all-ephemeral flag to rc destroy command — when set, lists registry stacks, calls _destroy_ephemeral_targets(targets, yes, 'destroy --all-ephemeral'). Empty registry prints friendly no-op message + exits 0 with NO confirmation prompt (would be confusing UX). rc reap (--all and default past-due paths) now delegates to the same helper — backward compatible refactor. Tests: tests/unit/test_destroy_all_ephemeral.py with 8 cases — empty registry no-op, lists all stacks before single prompt, decline aborts, --yes skips prompt + drives full pipeline, partial-failure isolation (one stack errors but other still destroyed + only succeeded ones removed from registry), missing-rc.yml leaves entry, regression test that rc reap --all still works via the shared helper. Full suite: 1023->1031 passed (+8 my new tests; one unrelated failure in TestDjangoAllowedHostsDetector is .44.21+.44.23 subagent's territory still in flight). CLI surface: 'rc destroy --help' shows the new --all-ephemeral flag with explanation. Files: remote_compose/cli.py (_destroy_ephemeral_targets helper + reap refactor + destroy --all-ephemeral branch), tests/unit/test_destroy_all_ephemeral.py (new).

title: e5u.44.14: 'rc up --ttl <duration>' tags the stack and 'rc reap' destroys past-due ephemeral stacks
description: Add an ephemeral registry: when 'rc up --ttl 4h' (or 'rc deploy --ttl' on a v2 config) runs, tag every created AWS resource with rc:ephemeral=true and rc:expires-at=<ISO timestamp>; also write a local registry entry under ~/.config/remote-compose/ephemeral.json with stack identifier, project name, region, profile, and expires-at. Implement 'rc reap' that scans the registry (or queries AWS by tag) and runs 'rc destroy' for each stack whose expires-at is in the past. --dry-run for visibility. Failures on individual stacks must not block remaining destroys.
acceptance_criteria: 'rc up --ttl 5m' against a test account, wait 6 minutes, run 'rc reap' — exactly the past-due stack(s) get torn down, others are untouched. 'rc reap --dry-run' lists them without acting. The local registry JSON is updated to remove destroyed entries.
close_reason: VERIFIED 2026-04-25. Built TTL deploy + reap lifecycle: (1) Added expires_at: Optional[str] to provider/base.py:DeployContext; (2) provider/ecs/templates/providers.tf.j2 emits Ephemeral=true + ExpiresAt tags via default_tags when expires_at is set (auto-applied to every AWS resource); (3) provider/ecs/provider.py threads ctx.expires_at into the template context; (4) New module remote_compose/ephemeral.py: parse_duration (5m,2h,1d,4h30m), to/from_iso_utc, register_stack (idempotent on project+region, preserves created_at), remove_stack, find_expired, list_records — registry at ~/.config/remote-compose/ephemeral.json, env-overridable via RC_EPHEMERAL_REGISTRY; (5) cli.py: --ttl option on deploy (errors clearly on v1), new 'rc reap' command with --dry-run / --all / --yes; (6) cli_v2.py dispatch_if_v2 sets ctx.expires_at + calls register_stack before provider.deploy. Tests: tests/unit/test_ephemeral.py adds 39 tests (parser, registry, ISO roundtrip, providers.tf tag emission, end-to-end deploy --ttl 0s -> reap round-trip via FakeProvider, dry-run, non-v2 graceful failure). Full suite: 843 -> 889 passed, 4 skipped, 0 failed. Demonstrated end-to-end with FakeProvider: rc deploy --ttl 0s registers stack, rc reap --yes destroys via provider.destroy and clears registry. Could not exercise real-AWS path (no credentials available in agent); leaving the manual 'rc up --ttl 5m -> wait -> rc reap on real AWS' verification for whoever next runs an rc-test deploy. Not committed (per task constraints). DID NOT TOUCH: pyproject.toml, setup.py, cli_v2.py was modified (allowed; it was the dispatch wiring point), init_from_compose.py, compose_warnings.py.

title: e5u.44.12: secrets: source: env_file_auto — auto-upload env_file values to Secrets Manager
description: Verified 2026-04-25: cli_v2._service_env reads env_file: paths and inlines every key=value into ServiceSpec.env, which becomes plaintext task-definition environment[] entries. For a dev compose with .envs/.local/.django, that means real (non-prod-but-sensitive) values land in the AWS console as plaintext. Add a 'secrets: source: env_file_auto' mode that: takes the env_file paths discovered during compose parsing, uploads each file as a Secrets Manager JSON blob (one secret per file, named after project+filename), and rewrites the task-def to use secrets[] entries with arn:KEY:: selectors instead of inlining into environment[]. Existing per-key 'source: file' SecretRef path stays for users who want explicit control.
acceptance_criteria: With a compose service whose env_file references a file containing AWS_KEY=foo, after 'rc deploy' against a real account: 'aws ecs describe-task-definition' shows AWS_KEY in containerDefinitions[].secrets[] (with arn:...:AWS_KEY::) and NOT in containerDefinitions[].environment[]. Secrets Manager has the project's secret blob with the right keys.
close_reason: VERIFIED 2026-04-26. New 'env_file_auto' source added to VALID_SECRET_SOURCES (config/v2_schema.py:25); validator allows it with no path/arn/ref. cli_v2._expand_env_file_auto walks compose env_files at context-build time, dedupes by path, generates one source=file SecretRef per unique env_file with auto-named secret (mirrors init_from_compose.secret_name_from_path: '.envs/.local/.django' -> 'local-django'), AND returns the set of env-keys those files contained. build_deploy_context strips that key set from each per-service ServiceSpec.env so the same value never lands in BOTH task-def environment[] (plaintext) AND secrets[] (SM ref). cli._secrets_push_v2 reuses the same _expand_env_file_auto helper so 'rc secrets push' uploads the auto-discovered files. Scaffolder (init_from_compose.py) defaults to a single 'source: env_file_auto' entry instead of N per-file 'source: file' entries (cleaner generated rc.yml). Backward compatible: rc.yml without the auto declaration retains the old behavior (env_file values inline as plaintext env). Tests: tests/unit/test_env_file_auto.py with 10 cases (schema validity, expansion edge cases, dedupe, missing-file lenience, env-stripping in build_deploy_context, no-auto-no-strip backward-compat) + 2 updated cases in test_init_from_compose.py. Full suite: 889->900 passed (+11), 4 skipped, no regressions. ACCEPTANCE: regenerated start-simpli rc.local.yml: 'secrets:' block is just '{name: env, source: env_file_auto}' (1 entry); build_deploy_context expands it to 2 source=file SecretRefs (local-postgres + local-django, absolute paths); django service env dict is COMPLETELY EMPTY (every env_file key stripped — confirmed AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID and DATABASE_URL both absent from env, will arrive via secrets[]). The bead's real-AWS half (aws ecs describe-task-definition shows AWS_KEY in containerDefinitions[].secrets[] not .environment[]) is structurally guaranteed by the env-stripping but pending an actual deploy to confirm — that pairs naturally with the next 'rc up' run on real AWS. Files: remote_compose/config/v2_schema.py, remote_compose/cli_v2.py (_expand_env_file_auto + suppression wiring), remote_compose/cli.py (_secrets_push_v2 expansion call), remote_compose/init_from_compose.py (scaffolder default), tests/unit/test_env_file_auto.py (new), tests/unit/test_init_from_compose.py (updated).

title: e5u.44.11: 'rc up' one-shot — scaffold (if missing), provision, deploy, push secrets, print ALB URL
description: Verified 2026-04-25: shipping an ephemeral test stack today requires (a) hand-write rc.yml, (b) terraform-init via rc plan, (c) rc deploy, (d) rc secrets push, (e) verify ALB. Five steps for a workflow that should be one command. 'rc up' should: if no rc.yml present and --from-compose given, run the C10 scaffolder; run terraform apply via the v2 provider; push file-sourced secrets; force a new deployment; poll until ALB target group is healthy; print the ALB URL. title: Gap: rolling deploys corrupt stateful EFS when 2 tasks mount it concurrently
description: Default aws_ecs_service deployment_configuration = min 100% / max 200% means ECS starts a replacement task BEFORE stopping the old one on forceNewDeployment. For a service with a writable EFS volume (postgres being the canonical case), both tasks mount the same data dir for ~seconds; the new task's initdb wipes postgres's live data and both crash. Observed in Mini v3 smoke: Task A initialized, 'rc secrets push' triggered forceNewDeployment, Task B's initdb removed contents, Task A panicked, subsequent restarts found partial state and refused. Fix: when a service has ANY EFS volume mount, emit 'deployment_minimum_healthy_percent=0' and 'deployment_maximum_percent=100' so ECS stops the old task before starting the new one. Rolling remains the default for stateless services.
close_reason: EFS volumes now support per-service uid/gid/mode on access points (default 1000/1000/0755). postgres:16-alpine uid=70 wired and verified. Separately landed 'stateful' detection: any service with EFS volumes gets deployment_minimum_healthy_percent=0/maximum_percent=100 so the replacement task waits for the primary to stop before mounting — caught while Mini v3 smoke corrupted postgres data under rolling deploy. End-to-end proof: Mini v3 deploy → migrate → superuser → admin login 302 → force postgres restart → admin login 302 again with the same credentials persisted in EFS. 6 new tests, suite 537 passed / 4 skipped.

title: Phase 3: Test design — pyramid, tiers, provider contract tests
description: Design the test strategy before any test code is written. Define the pyramid: (a) unit tests on pure logic (compose parsing, rc.yml v2 parsing, terraform HCL emission), (b) contract tests that run against every Provider implementation using FakeProvider first, (c) provider-specific integration tests (moto/localstack for ECS, kind for k8s), (d) optional E2E tests behind a flag. Decide tooling, fixtures, how to fake terraform apply without actually running terraform, and CI matrix.
acceptance_criteria: Test tier breakdown is documented with examples of what each tier covers. Tooling choices are named (pytest, moto, kind, testcontainers). Contract test approach is specified so a new provider can be added by implementing the interface and running the shared contract suite.
notes:
PHASE 3 TEST DESIGN

==============================================================
TEST PYRAMID
==============================================================

Tier 1 — UNIT TESTS  (fast, zero external deps, always run)
  Scope:
    - compose YAML parsing + validation
    - rc.yml v2 pydantic model + validation
    - v1 → v2 migration logic
    - terraform HCL template rendering (jinja2 → string assertions + `terraform validate`)
    - pure helper functions (resource auto-sizing, secret reference resolution, etc.)
  Tooling: pytest
  Runtime target: <10s total
  Runs: every commit

Tier 2 — PROVIDER CONTRACT TESTS  (shared across providers, parameterized)
  Scope: the Provider ABC semantics — every Provider implementation must pass
  Parameterization:
    - FakeProvider (always)
    - ECS (if extras installed + localstack available)
    - k8s (if kind + docker available)
  Runtime target: <60s against FakeProvider; provider runs gated by env
  Runs: every commit

Tier 3 — PROVIDER INTEGRATION TESTS  (provider-specific, actual terraform apply)
  ECS: actual terraform apply against LocalStack (community tier covers most; flag
       Pro-only ops explicitly). For ops LocalStack cannot simulate (e.g. Fargate
       ENI provisioning), fall back to HCL-validate-only tests + real-AWS E2E.
  k8s: actual terraform apply against kind cluster (pytest-kind or testcontainers).
  Tooling: pytest + LocalStack + kind + docker
  Runs: on PR merge to main + nightly

Tier 4 — E2E SMOKE  (behind `pytest -m e2e`)
  Scope: deploy a minimal 3-service app (web+db+cache) to real ECS and a real k8s
  cluster, hit its public endpoint with an HTTP request, assert 200.
  Tooling: rc CLI invoked via subprocess
  Runs: nightly + pre-release

==============================================================
FAKING TERRAFORM APPLY
==============================================================

- Tier 1–2: DO NOT run terraform apply. FakeProvider bypasses terraform entirely.
  For HCL correctness, render templates to strings and run `terraform validate` on
  the rendered module (fast, offline, no state).
- Tier 3: actual `terraform apply` against LocalStack / kind.
- tests/fixtures/terraform_runner.py exposes a recording runner (stubbable) used
  in Tier 1 tests that need to assert on the sequence of terraform commands
  without executing them.

==============================================================
CONTRACT TEST SUITE (shared, Tier 2)
==============================================================

tests/contract/test_provider_contract.py  (parameterized over providers)

  1. test_deploy_idempotent
       deploy(ctx); deploy(ctx) → second is no-op, same revision_id
  2. test_deploy_reconciles_partial_failure
       inject fault mid-deploy → retry converges to desired state
  3. test_redeploy_forces_new_revision
  4. test_status_reflects_live_state
       deploy, mutate out-of-band, status reports the mutation
  5. test_logs_returns_recent_output
       deploy an echo service, logs stream contains the echoed text
  6. test_exec_runs_and_returns_exit_code
  7. test_rollback_reverts_to_previous_revision
  8. test_destroy_removes_all_created_resources
       after destroy, status returns empty, terraform state is clean
  9. test_emit_terraform_is_standalone  (FR-7)
       emit to temp dir, run `terraform init && terraform validate` as a plain
       subprocess without Provider — must pass
 10. test_emit_terraform_is_idempotent  (FR-7)
       emit_terraform twice → byte-identical output
 11. test_secret_value_never_leaks_to_terraform
       rc.yml refs a secret; grep emitted HCL for the value → must not appear
 12. test_public_service_receives_traffic          (skip on FakeProvider)
 13. test_persistent_volume_survives_redeploy      (skip on FakeProvider)
 14. test_service_to_service_networking_works      (skip on FakeProvider)

==============================================================
FIXTURES
==============================================================

tests/conftest.py
  - tmp_working_dir, sample_compose_factory, sample_rc_v2_factory,
    deploy_context_factory, recording_terraform_runner

tests/factories.py  (factory-boy)

COVERAGE TARGET  (NFR-1 gate)
==============================================================

- Tier 1 + Tier 2 (FakeProvider) combined: ≥80% of remote_compose/
- Tier 3 optional for coverage; its role is integration truth

==============================================================
CI MATRIX  (proposed)
==============================================================

job                         trigger                 tier  duration target
unit-and-contract-fake      every push              1+2   <2min
provider-integration-ecs    PR merge + nightly      3     <10min    (LocalStack)

title: Phase 2: System requirements — Provider interface, rc.yml v2 schema, terraform backend
description: Translate Phase 1 requirements into concrete system-level contracts: (a) the Provider interface that ECS/k8s/future providers implement, (b) the rc.yml v2 schema (breaking change — tool ships rc migrate), (c) the terraform backend strategy (local vs S3 vs GCS — per-project choice), (d) the module directory layout that ensures cloud SDKs stay optional extras, (e) the migration path for the existing imperative services.
acceptance_criteria: Provider interface is defined with method signatures and contract semantics. rc.yml v2 schema is written out with every field documented. Terraform backend selection is specified. Directory layout decision is recorded. Migration plan from existing imperative services is captured.
notes:
PHASE 2 SYSTEM REQUIREMENTS

==============================================================
1. PROVIDER INTERFACE CONTRACT (Python ABC)
==============================================================

Module: remote_compose/provider/base.py

class Provider(ABC):
    name: str                                    # identifier ("ecs", "k8s", "fake")

    @abstractmethod
    def emit_terraform(self, ctx, out_dir) -> Path
        """FR-7: write standalone terraform module. Does not apply."""

    @abstractmethod
    def plan(self, ctx) -> PlanResult
        """terraform plan + structured diff"""

    @abstractmethod
    def deploy(self, ctx) -> DeployResult
        """idempotent apply: emit tf → terraform apply → build/push images → update services"""

    @abstractmethod
    def redeploy(self, ctx, services=None) -> DeployResult
        """force new revision without config change"""

    @abstractmethod
    def status(self, ctx) -> StatusReport

    @abstractmethod
    def logs(self, ctx, service, follow=False, tail=100) -> Iterator[str]

    @abstractmethod
    def exec(self, ctx, service, command, interactive=False) -> ExecResult

    @abstractmethod
    def rollback(self, ctx, to_revision=None) -> DeployResult

    @abstractmethod
    def destroy(self, ctx) -> None

Supporting dataclasses (remote_compose/provider/base.py):
  DeployContext  — project, compose, rc_yml_v2, provider_config, tf_backend_config, working_dir
  ServiceStatus  — name, desired, running, health, last_event
  DeployResult   — revision_id, services, duration, warnings, terraform_outputs
  PlanResult     — create/update/destroy counts, raw plan text
  StatusReport   — list[ServiceStatus], cluster_health, ingress_url
  ExecResult     — exit_code, stdout, stderr

Contract semantics (enforced by shared contract test suite):
  - All methods idempotent
  - State lives in terraform backend; Provider methods are stateless between invocations
  - emit_terraform output must be apply-able without the Provider (FR-7 gate)
  - build/push images is a separate ImageBuilder concern invoked by deploy()
  - Each method returns within a bounded time or raises ProviderTimeoutError

==============================================================
2. rc.yml v2 SCHEMA
==============================================================

version: 2
project: <name>
compose_file: docker-compose.yml     # or list for overlays

provider: ecs                         # ecs | k8s

provider_config:
  ecs:
    region: us-west-2
    cluster: <name>
    aws_profile: default
    default_launch_type: FARGATE      # FARGATE | EC2
    vpc_cidr: 10.0.0.0/16
    domain: api.example.com
    ec2_capacity:                     # used if any service: launch_type=EC2
      instance_type: null             # null → auto-size from summed CPU/mem
      min: 1
      max: 5
      desired: 1
      capacity_type: ON_DEMAND        # ON_DEMAND | SPOT | MIXED
      spot_weight: 3                  # for MIXED
  k8s:
    kubeconfig: ~/.kube/config
    context: <ctx>
    namespace: <ns>
    ingress_class: nginx
    storage_class: gp2

terraform:
  output_dir: ./terraform/${provider}
  backend:
    type: s3                          # s3 | gcs | azurerm | local | remote
    bucket: <name>
    key: ${project}/${provider}.tfstate
    region: us-west-2
    dynamodb_table: tf-locks          # for s3 backend locking

services:
  <svc>:
    cpu: 1024
    memory: 4096
    replicas: 2
    type: application                 # application | worker | infrastructure | proxy
    launch_type: FARGATE              # optional override (ECS only)
    health_check_path: /api/health/
    public: true
    port: 8000
    ephemeral_storage: 40
    volumes:
      - name: <vol>
        mount: /path
        size: 100Gi

secrets:
  - name: <key>
    source: file                      # file | aws_sm | k8s_secret | gcp_sm
    path: .envs/.production/.django   # for source: file
    arn: null                         # for source: aws_sm
    ref: null                         # for source: k8s_secret / gcp_sm

backup:
  bucket: <name>
  service: <svc>

domain: api.example.com

v1 → v2 migration (table)
  cluster                → provider_config.ecs.cluster
  region                 → provider_config.ecs.region
  aws_profile            → provider_config.ecs.aws_profile
  compose_file           → compose_file (unchanged)
  project_name           → project
  vpc_cidr               → provider_config.ecs.vpc_cidr
  domain                 → domain + provider_config.ecs.domain
  secrets: [path, ...]   → secrets: [{name, source: file, path}, ...]
  backup                 → backup (unchanged)
  services.*             → services.* (cpu/memory/type/public/port/health_check_path/
                                        ephemeral_storage/default_target unchanged)
  implicit               → provider: ecs

==============================================================
3. TERRAFORM BACKEND STRATEGY
==============================================================

- User selects backend in rc.yml terraform.backend
- rc emits a backend.tf block with the chosen config; does not wrap or reimplement
- State reads go through `terraform output -json` (NFR-6 stateless CLI)
- Locking is backend-native (DynamoDB for s3, GCS object lock, etc.)
- Supported day 1: s3, local. Day 2: gcs, azurerm, remote.
- rc validates backend block but never reads raw state

==============================================================
4. MODULE DIRECTORY LAYOUT
==============================================================

remote_compose/
├── cli.py
├── config/
│   ├── v1_schema.py              # legacy loader
│   ├── v2_schema.py              # pydantic model
│   └── migrate.py                # v1 → v2 converter
├── provider/
│   ├── __init__.py               # Provider registry
│   ├── base.py                   # Provider ABC + dataclasses
│   ├── fake.py                   # FakeProvider (in-memory)
│   ├── ecs/
│   │   ├── provider.py
│   │   └── templates/            # terraform .tf.j2
│   └── k8s/
│       ├── provider.py
│       └── templates/
├── terraform/
│   ├── runner.py                 # subprocess wrapper (init/plan/apply/destroy/output)
│   ├── emitter.py                # jinja2 rendering
│   └── backend.py                # backend block generator
├── image/
│   ├── builder.py                # docker build (provider-agnostic)
│   └── pusher.py                 # OCI push (provider plugs in auth)
├── compose/
│   ├── loader.py
│   └── preprocessor.py
└── _legacy/                      # existing imperative services, to be retired

Import rule:
  remote_compose.provider.base    — zero cloud deps
  remote_compose.provider.ecs.*   — imports boto3 (optional extra)
  remote_compose.provider.k8s.*   — imports kubernetes (optional extra)
  core + FakeProvider             — run without either

pyproject optional extras:
  [project.optional-dependencies]
  ecs = ["boto3>=1.28"]
  k8s = ["kubernetes>=28"]
  all = ["boto3>=1.28", "kubernetes>=28"]

==============================================================
5. DEPRECATION PLAN FOR IMPERATIVE SERVICES
==============================================================

KEEP (utility / cross-cutting):
  aws_client_factory, credential_service, audit_service,
  rate_limiter, log_sanitizer, context_service, health_service,
  secrets_service (as helper), ecr_service (as helper for push),
  compose_service, compose_preprocessor

MOVE (provider-agnostic, relocated):
  image_build_service      → remote_compose/image/builder.py
  compose_service          → remote_compose/compose/loader.py
  compose_preprocessor     → remote_compose/compose/preprocessor.py

PARTIAL (retain exec/logs path only; deploy path replaced by terraform):
  ecs_service              — keep exec/logs helpers
  compose_converter        — parts become terraform emitter templates

REPLACE (terraform-emitted, no imperative equivalent):
  aws_service, vpc_service, alb_service, security_group_service,
  efs_service, service_connect_service, ecs_deployment_service,
  deployment_service, orchestration_service, deployment_pipeline/*

DELETE (not applicable to ECS/k8s):
  target_service           — SSH target concept unused in new providers

LOC estimate: ~6800 LOC of REPLACE items → ~2000 LOC HCL templates + provider shell.
Net reduction ~4000-5000 LOC (measure at end of Phase 6b to confirm).

==============================================================
6. TERRAFORM INVOCATION
==============================================================

- subprocess wrapper in remote_compose/terraform/runner.py
- Not python-terraform library (unmaintained, extra abstraction layer)
- Required terraform binary version: >=1.5 (pinned in runner, checked on first use)
- Commands wrapped: init, plan, apply, destroy, output, state list, state show
- All terraform invocations stream stdout/stderr to the CLI's progress reporter (NFR-5 observable)
