title: e5u.44.8: 'rc plan' warns when container configs reference host.docker.internal or other non-VPC-resolvable hosts
description: Verified 2026-04-25: start-simpli's nginx.conf has multiple 'server host.docker.internal:NNNN;' upstreams (landing, raise-app, recipesimpli, etc.). In ECS those hosts are unreachable; nginx returns 502 for those routes with no clear signal at deploy time. Scan files referenced by COPY in build contexts (or, more practically, any text file mounted into the image at known paths like nginx.conf) for host.docker.internal and similar dev-only DNS names; emit warnings during plan. Stretch: also warn on hostnames that are not compose service names AND not resolvable as public DNS.
acceptance_criteria: A fixture nginx.conf containing 'server host.docker.internal:3000;' triggers a warning during 'rc plan' that names the file path and the offending host. False-positive control: localhost / 127.0.0.1 do not trigger.
close_reason: VERIFIED 2026-04-25. Implemented detect_bad_hosts in remote_compose/compose_warnings.py. For each compose service with a build:{context}, scans <ctx>/**/nginx.conf and <ctx>/**/*.conf (capped at 32 files, 256KB/file) for the literal 'host.docker.internal'. Test: PYTHONPATH=. .venv/bin/pytest tests/unit/test_compose_warnings.py::TestBadHostDetector -v -> 4 passed. test_nginx_conf_with_host_docker_internal_warns asserts warning contains the file path and 'host.docker.internal' and 'nginx'. test_localhost_does_not_trigger is the false-positive control (localhost AND 127.0.0.1 produce zero warnings). test_no_build_context_skips_scan + test_nested_conf_files_scanned cover edge cases. End-to-end via TestRcPlanRendersWarnings::test_host_docker_internal_warning_appears_in_plan. Full suite: 843 passed, 4 skipped. NOTE: stretch goal (hostname not a compose service AND not public DNS) deferred — heuristic too noisy without DNS lookup; primary acceptance criterion met.

title: copilot.7: multi-environment handling — pick one or emit per-env files
description: Copilot env-specific overrides live in service manifests under 'environments.<env>:' blocks. CLI options: --env staging selects one environment and emits a single rc.yml; --env all emits rc.<env>.yml per environment. Default: pick the most-prod-looking env (production > staging > dev) with an explicit warning. Tests cover both modes.
close_reason: apply_environment_overrides(svc, env) returns a NEW CopilotService with manifest's environments.<env> overrides deep-merged onto base raw dict. Per-key deep merge (nested dicts merge recursively, scalars and lists replace wholesale). Drops the environments key from the merged output so downstream translators don't re-process. Never mutates input — translators can iterate the same base manifest for multiple envs. 13 new tests covering scalar overrides, nested dict merges (image, http, storage), variables/secrets per-env, missing env / null env / no env block paths, and immutability.

title: copilot.6: variables → compose environment + secrets → rc.yml secrets
description: Copilot 'variables: { KEY: value }' → docker-compose service environment: dict (literal values, no SM lookup). Copilot 'secrets: { KEY: { secretsmanager: ARN } }' → rc.yml secrets section pointing at source=aws_sm + arn. Copilot's '${COPILOT_ENVIRONMENT_NAME}' interpolation in secret ARNs has to be resolved per environment — leave as a templated value when --env not specified, hard-code when --env is given. Test both paths.
close_reason: translate_env_and_secrets maps Copilot variables: → compose service.environment dict (values stringified, compose requires strings). Copilot secrets: → rc.yml v2 secrets list with source=aws_sm + arn. Supports both long form ({secretsmanager: arn} / {ssm: arn}) and short string form (KEY: arn). ${COPILOT_ENVIRONMENT_NAME} substitution: stays literal when env=None (multi-env handoff to 43.7), inline-replaced when env is given. Secrets preserve declaration order. 10 new tests; 701 passed / 4 skipped.

title: rawcompose.C: handle compose ports: array — multi-port intra-VPC exposure
description: Compose 'ports: [7788:7788, 5901:5901, 5902:5902]' maps several TCP ports. Today provider only emits the FIRST port for ALB ingress. Fix: when a service is private (no public:true), every port in compose ports[] becomes a containerPort in the task def + the tasks SG already accepts intra-VPC traffic so other services can reach all of them. When a service is public, only one ALB target makes sense — pick the first or require an explicit alb_port field. Test-first.
close_reason: Provider now respects compose 'build.target' (passed to docker build --target), 'env_file:' (single string or list, paths relative to compose dir, merged in declaration order with environment: dict winning), and compose 'ports:' arrays (primary port goes to ALB target group when public, every additional port lands in the task def's portMappings as intra-VPC accessible). 11 new unit tests; 626 passed / 4 skipped.

title: autoimport.3: rc compose import CLI scaffolds an rc.yml from a compose file
description: rc compose import [--from <compose-file>] [--out rc.yml] [--exclude svc1,svc2] [--project NAME]. Reads compose, writes a v2 rc.yml with project+provider+services blocks pre-filled. Sensible defaults: cpu/memory by service hint (db services get more memory, workers get less cpu). For services with ports[]: marks public=true + sets port. Adds inline comments with TODO markers (e.g., domain, secrets). Tests use temp compose fixtures.
close_reason: rc compose import --exclude shipped. Drops named compose services to compose.exclude; validates each name exists; CSV form on CLI. 4 new tests pass + existing 13 unchanged. The auto-import scaffolder is now feature-complete per the bead description (--from / --out / --project / --exclude / --force).

title: Followup: provider.deploy two-phase apply when destroying TGs referenced by listeners
description: When a default-target service gains its own domain, the old aws_lb_target_group.default needs to drop. AWS rejects 'delete TG while in use' if terraform schedules the listener update + TG delete in the same plan. Terraform requires a manual two-pass: 'terraform apply -target=aws_lb_listener.https' then full apply. Provider should detect the situation (state delta on default TG) and run the listener-only apply automatically before the main one.

title: UX: rc secrets push should update task defs when new keys appear in env files
description: Today: 'rc secrets push' uploads new key values to SM and force-rolls services. But the task def's secrets[] block enumerates KEYS individually with arn:KEY:: selectors. Adding a NEW key to .envs/.foo/.django uploads it to SM, but the task def doesn't reference it, so the container never sees it. Workaround: 'rc deploy --no-build' after every push that introduces new keys. Fix: rc secrets push should detect new keys (compare current file keys vs task def secrets[] names) and trigger a task-def re-emit + force-deploy automatically. Or document the two-step requirement.

title: Followup: ECSProvider.deploy should auto-import the orphan container-insights log group when present
description: When upgrading from a stack deployed before terraform managed the container-insights log group, terraform apply fails with ResourceAlreadyExistsException because AWS auto-created the log group during the previous deploy. Workaround: 'terraform import aws_cloudwatch_log_group.container_insights /aws/ecs/containerinsights/<cluster>/performance' once. Real fix: provider.deploy detects the situation via boto3 before apply, runs import as a sub-step. Or: render an aws_cloudwatch_log_group with lifecycle.create_before_destroy=true and prevent_destroy=false plus a data lookup, swallowing the conflict at apply time.

title: cleanup.D: rc audit — post-destroy AWS-side cleanup verification
description: Sweep across the resource classes terraform manages — ECS clusters, VPCs by Project tag, ALBs, target groups, EFS, ECR, service discovery namespaces, log groups, IAM roles by name prefix, secrets, security groups, S3 buckets — and report any leftovers tagged with the project name. Optional --delete to clean orphans. Useful both as a destroy verifier and as an account-hygiene check.
close_reason: rc audit sweeps 12 AWS resource classes (ECS clusters, VPCs by Project tag, ALBs, target groups, EFS, ECR, service discovery namespaces, log groups, IAM roles by name prefix, secrets, security groups, S3 buckets) for resources matching a project name. Pure function audit_project(session, project, region) → AuditReport with typed findings + grouped render. Defensive _safe wrapper short-circuits on missing API permissions OR mocked-not-iterable returns. CLI wraps with rc.yml resolution: --project/--region/--profile auto-derive from rc.yml v2 provider_config when omitted. --delete is currently dry-run (per-resource deletion ordering is non-trivial; defer). Live verified: rc audit on sentinal-test stack found exactly 22 resources across 12 classes matching what's deployed. 15 new tests; 746 passed / 4 skipped.

title: cleanup.C: rc db dump-local --container wraps docker exec pg_dump
description: Standardize the local-side dump for rc db push. Resolves the docker container by name, reads its POSTGRES_USER/DB/PORT env, runs pg_dump -Fc, writes to a default path under /tmp/rc-dumps/<project>-<timestamp>.dump unless --to is given. Saves users from remembering port quirks (sentinal listens on 5434, not 5432) and quoting.
close_reason: rc db dump-local --container <name> [--to <path>] [--user/db/port overrides] wraps docker exec pg_dump. Pure inspect_container_env() + dump_local() helpers in remote_compose.dblocal so tests inject mocks. Auto-discovers POSTGRES_USER/DB/PORT from container env (no more remembering sentinal's 5434 quirk). Default output path: /tmp/rc-dumps/<project>-<iso-timestamp>.dump where project is read from rc.yml v2 if present. CLI prints user/db/port/size and a 'Next: rc db push <path>' hint to chain the full local→remote seed flow. Live verified against sentinal_postgres: produced a 570 MB dump with 164 TABLE DATA entries, byte-identical pg_restore --list output to the manual docker exec pg_dump command we used to run by hand. 11 new tests; 757 passed / 4 skipped.

title: sentinal.F: rc deploy should wait for tasks healthy before running auto_on_deploy hooks
description: Mini v4 surfaced this: cold deploy + auto_on_deploy migrate fails because tasks are still rolling with placeholder secrets. Fix by polling describe-services rolloutState=COMPLETED with a timeout before running hooks. If not healthy in N minutes, skip hooks with a clear warning pointing to 'rc lifecycle <hook>' as the fallback.

title: sentinal.D: dump local sentinal_postgres to .dump file
description: docker exec sentinal_postgres pg_dump -Fc -U $POSTGRES_USER $POSTGRES_DB > /tmp/sentinal-rc/sentinal-dump.dump. Verify size + sample with pg_restore --list. This is the baseline test fixture for rc db push.
close_reason: 569 MB local pg_dump from sentinal_postgres container (postgres 17.2 source). 2124 TOC entries, 164 table-data entries. Stored at /tmp/sentinal-rc/sentinal-dump.dump.

title: lifecycle.7: framework presets — django, rails, phoenix, laravel
description: If a service declares 'framework: django' (and the lifecycle dict is absent or partial), inject sensible defaults: migrate, createsuperuser, collectstatic, shell. Same for rails (db:migrate, db:seed, console), phoenix (ecto.migrate), laravel (migrate, db:seed). Users can override per-hook in rc.yml.
close_reason: Framework lifecycle hooks shipped on top of .47's registry. django/rails/phoenix presets each carry a lifecycle_hooks dict; cli_v2 merges into ServiceSpec.lifecycle for hooks the user hasn't declared. Explicit framework: field on ServiceV2 (default detect_framework() resolves it). User overrides always win. Interactive hooks (shell/console/dbshell) get interactive=True. 12 new tests + 22 framework + cli_v2 backward-compat = green.

title: Ergonomics: ECS execute-command silently swallows script stdout from non-TTY
description: aws ecs execute-command invoked with 'tail -f /dev/null | ...' (required to keep stdin open from Claude Code Bash tool) reliably swallows stdout from non-trivial scripts. Simple commands like 'curl | tail' work, but base64-decoded scripts with pipes, heredocs, or stdout-to-file show an empty output file even when the script clearly ran to completion (verified by side effects). Affects debugging and any validation that relies on stdout. Workarounds tried: redirect inside container to /tmp/x.log then cat; still empty. Root cause likely in the SSM agent's handling of stdout when the local client disconnects too fast after the shell exits. Investigate: (a) explicit flush/sleep at script end, (b) write results to S3 via presigned URL and fetch locally, (c) have rc exec open a proper pty via script/expect.

title: Mini v1b-admin: public django admin URL + superuser
description: Flip django to public default ALB target, run migrations, create superuser via env vars. Hand user a clickable URL to verify admin login works end-to-end against the real start-simpli-api image.
acceptance_criteria: curl http://<alb>/admin/login/ returns 200; user logs in via browser with handed creds.
close_reason: Mini v1b-admin acceptance met. Flipped django to public default ALB target (nginx stays internal), added DJANGO_SUPERUSER_* env vars, pulled latest start-simpli-api main (c3ba15d → e5c7369), rc deploy cold 311.7s → redeploy 64.4s after CSRF_TRUSTED_ORIGINS update for new ALB hostname. aws ecs execute-command migrate → all 79 migrations applied OK. createsuperuser --noinput → exit 0. User confirmed login works via browser at http://<alb>/admin/login/. Key finding: USERNAME_FIELD='email' on start-simpli User model, so the admin form field is Email not Username — relevant for any future automation. Destroy clean (one orphan container-insights log group, matches rc-e5u.12, separately tracked).

title: Gap: ECS service template missing enable_execute_command
description: aws_ecs_service.enable_execute_command is not set, so 'aws ecs execute-command' fails with InvalidParameterException on v2-deployed tasks. Needed for rc exec (legacy and v2), rc db backup/restore (which uses execute-command), and internal-service health verification from another container. Task role already has the permissions (ssmmessages:CreateControlChannel etc via managed AmazonSSMManagedInstanceCore — actually need to verify). Fix: add 'enable_execute_command = true' to aws_ecs_service block in services.tf.j2, and ensure the task_role IAM policy permits ssmmessages:CreateControlChannel, OpenControlChannel, CreateDataChannel, OpenDataChannel.

title: Mini v5: backup/restore round-trip in us-west-1
description: Depends on rc-e5u.28.4 decision. If provider path: create 'ss-migration-test-db-dumps' in us-west-1, backup Mini v3 postgres, destroy, redeploy, restore, verify row count. If legacy path: run 'rc backup' against test stack.

title: Mini v4: throwaway subdomain + ACM + R53 wiring
description: Use 'migration-test.startsimpli.com' (pre-create R53 zone if not delegated). Enable domain block in v2 yaml. Goal: ACM cert issues, ALB serves HTTPS, external curl returns 200. Tear down subdomain after.

title: Mini v3: postgres EFS persistence survives redeploy
description: After Mini v2 green, add EFS volume + mount for postgres in v2 yaml (resolve rc-e5u.28.2 first). Load test data, force task restart, verify data is still there. Validates EFS access point uid mapping on fresh us-west-1 stack.
close_reason: EFS volumes now support per-service uid/gid/mode on access points (default 1000/1000/0755). postgres:16-alpine uid=70 wired and verified. Separately landed 'stateful' detection: any service with EFS volumes gets deployment_minimum_healthy_percent=0/maximum_percent=100 so the replacement task waits for the primary to stop before mounting — caught while Mini v3 smoke corrupted postgres data under rolling deploy. End-to-end proof: Mini v3 deploy → migrate → superuser → admin login 302 → force postgres restart → admin login 302 again with the same credentials persisted in EFS. 6 new tests, suite 537 passed / 4 skipped.

title: Mini v1: real images pushed + services boot
description: Build start-simpli-api images from HEAD of migration test branch, push to us-west-1 ECR, redeploy. Goal: containers actually start (not crashlooping), django /api/health/ returns 200 via internal discovery. Still no real secrets. Depends on Mini v0.
close_reason: Mini v1a acceptance met with three provider fixes along the way. (1) ImageBuilder bug: relative dockerfile resolved against cwd instead of build context — fixed + test added. (2) Missing enable_execute_command on aws_ecs_service — added to template. (3) Missing ssmmessages:* on task role — added IAM policy. Django real image built + pushed to us-west-1 ECR (linux/amd64 cross-build). Deploy: 106s cold, 52s redeploy. 7/7 healthy. curl /api/v1/health/ via ecs execute-command → HTTP 200. Full suite 509 passed / 4 skipped.

title: Mini v0: us-west-1 stack-up smoke for ss migration
description: Deploy migrated v2 rc.yml to us-west-1 as project 'rc-test-ss-migration' with placeholder env values, no real secrets, no domain. Goal: terraform init/apply clean, all 7 services reach RUNNING. Zero touch of us-west-2 prod. Depends on rc-e5u.28.1.
acceptance_criteria: rc deploy exits 0; rc status shows 7/7 RUNNING; rc destroy cleans up.
close_reason: Mini v0 acceptance met. rc deploy 204s → 7 services, rc status 7/7 healthy, curl ALB → HTTP 200 (nginx default, 896B). rc destroy + independent AWS verify: all 11 resource classes empty in us-west-1 except 1 orphan container-insights log group (separately tracked). us-west-2 ss-debuggai-prod cluster untouched. Real issues surfaced: (1) postgres EFS chown = known rc-e5u.27 (worked around by dropping volume for v0), (2) nginx:alpine returns 404 on /health (worked around with health_check_path: /; real nginx image will serve /health in v1).

title: Mini v2: test secrets wired
description: Create throwaway .envs/.test/ secret files (distinct from prod .envs/.production/). Redeploy. Goal: django boots with DATABASE_URL etc, celery picks up test tasks. Confirms Fernet-encrypted file→Secrets Manager wiring works end-to-end for all services.
close_reason: Provider now reads .env file KEY names at emit time (values never touched) and emits one secrets[] entry per key with ECS JSON-key syntax 'arn:KEY::'. New v2-aware rc secrets push reads each file, uploads as JSON blob to the per-file SM secret, and force-rolls services. End-to-end Mini v2 deploy: 318s cold build, 7/7 degraded until 'rc secrets push', then 7/7 healthy; curl /admin/login/ → 200, full login POST → 302 Location: /admin/ using creds sourced entirely from SM. 21 new tests; full suite 531 passed / 4 skipped. Destroy clean.

title: Gap: backup config is parsed but unused by ECS provider
description: v2 BackupConfig (bucket, service) is parsed but provider ignores it. Current prod relies on legacy 'rc backup' CLI path (tied to v1 imperative services + sqlite state). Decide for v2: (a) provider emits an IAM policy attachment so task role can read/write the backup bucket, and CLI 'rc backup' resolves bucket from v2 yaml, or (b) keep backup tooling outside provider and document. Blocks Mini v5 only.
close_reason: Decision: keep backup tooling outside the ECS provider — the legacy CLI already works via host-side presigned URLs (task uses curl, no task-role IAM needed). Implemented a v2→legacy flatten shim in cli._load_config so 'rc db backup/restore/list' work against v2 rc.yml without touching the backup engine code. Unblocks Mini v5. Suite 506 passed / 4 skipped.

title: Gap: verify aws_profile is honored by ECS provider end-to-end
description: v2 schema stores provider_config.ecs.aws_profile. Need to confirm provider.emit_terraform + deploy/plan/status actually use this profile consistently (providers.tf.j2, boto3 calls). start-simpli uses profile 'debuggai' — if wiring is broken, migrated deploy would hit default credentials. Quick grep + one-line test.
close_reason: Verified: aws_profile is wired through both paths — providers.tf.j2 emits 'profile = ...' when set (already tested), and _default_session_factory passes it as profile_name to boto3 (new test added). Also added omission test. Suite: 495 passed / 4 skipped.

title: Gap: rc migrate doesn't emit EFS volumes for infrastructure services
description: v1 start-simpli runs postgres on EFS for persistence (legacy pipeline adds it). 'rc migrate' produces v2 yaml with NO volumes block, so migrated postgres would be ephemeral — data loss on task restart. Decide: (a) migrator auto-emits a volume + mount for postgres/redis when type=infrastructure, or (b) require explicit user annotation + document. Leaning (b) with a migrator WARNING printed whenever an infrastructure service is migrated without volumes. Must be fixed before Mini v3.
close_reason: Migrator emits an actionable warning when a type=infrastructure service is migrated without a volumes block — with a concrete mount-path suggestion for known stateful images (postgres/mysql/mariadb/redis/mongo). CLI surfaces on stderr. 8 new tests. Full suite 503 passed / 4 skipped.

title: Gap: ECS provider silently drops ephemeral_storage
description: v2 schema parses services[*].ephemeral_storage (int GB) but remote_compose/provider/ecs/provider.py line 172-190 doesn't copy it into svc_view, so services.tf.j2 never emits ephemeralStorage block. start-simpli's django needs 40GB; would silently boot at 20GB default. Fix: add ephemeral_storage to svc_view, emit 'ephemeral_storage { size_in_gib = N }' in aws_ecs_task_definition when set and launch_type=FARGATE (EC2 doesn't support it). Add unit test + golden snapshot update.
close_reason: Provider now copies ServiceSpec.ephemeral_storage into svc_view, validates FARGATE-only + 21-200 GiB range, template emits ephemeral_storage{} block. 7 new tests; full unit+contract 493 passed / 4 skipped.

title: Phase 7a: Migrate start-simpli-api rc.yml to v2 + cut over deploy pipeline
description: Today start-simpli-api uses rc.yml v1 and runs through the legacy imperative 15-step pipeline on main branch. The portable-deploy branch ships rc migrate + v2 Provider dispatch, both verified end-to-end against real AWS. Next step: actually migrate start-simpli to v2, validate the emitted terraform matches the current infrastructure, and cut the prod deploy over to the new provider without downtime.  Steps: (1) Run 'rc migrate' on start-simpli-api's rc.yml, review the v2 output; (2) Compare emitted terraform against the live ss-debuggai-prod stack (terraform import + diff, or side-by-side describe); (3) Decide on strategy (blue/green new cluster vs terraform state import of existing resources); (4) Dry-run the v2 deploy (rc plan) and verify zero destructive changes; (5) Execute cutover; (6) Retire the v1 legacy path from start-simpli's deploy tooling.
acceptance_criteria: start-simpli-api's rc.yml is v2, rc deploy works against the new provider in production, existing services keep running through the cutover, and the legacy v1 code path is no longer on the critical path for that project.

title: Phase 6b.15: EFS encryption broken on accounts without alias/aws/elasticfilesystem
description: Cloud smoke error: 'The specified KMS key could not be found.' AWS returns this when creating an encrypted EFS in an account that has never used EFS — the aws-managed alias/aws/elasticfilesystem key doesn't auto-create via API (only via console). Fix: default encrypted=false with a prominent comment that production users should set encrypted=true + specify kms_key_id. OR: have the provider create the alias via aws_kms_alias + aws_kms_key before the EFS. For now default to unencrypted since this is infrastructure a user inherits; compliance can override.
acceptance_criteria: Fresh account with no pre-existing EFS resources can run rc deploy and EFS creation succeeds without manual KMS setup.

title: Phase 6b.14: EC2 launch type needs NAT gateway OR public subnet placement
description: Cloud smoke against real AWS caught this: aws_autoscaling_group launches EC2 instances into private subnets (aws_subnet.private[*].id) but there's no NAT gateway. Instances have no internet path to pull the ECS agent, ECR images, or register with the cluster. ASG waits 10 min then times out. Options: (a) add NAT gateway (production-correct, ~$0.045/hr, needs reap support); (b) default to public subnets with associate_public_ip_address=true on the launch template network_interfaces block (simpler, cheaper, slightly less secure); (c) use VPC endpoints for ECS + ECR + S3 + CloudWatch (no NAT needed but more HCL). Recommend (b) as default with (a)/(c) opt-in via rc.yml.
acceptance_criteria: A fresh rc deploy with launch_type=EC2 brings the ASG instance healthy within 3 minutes and the worker service starts tasks. Reap script cleans up NAT gateway (if used) and all EC2 network artifacts.
notes: Expanded scope: NOT just EC2. Also Fargate tasks need internet path to pull ECR images (same root cause — no NAT in private subnets). Current fix: Fargate tasks placed in PUBLIC subnets with assign_public_ip=true + tasks SG restricting inbound to ALB SG + self. Cost savings: ~$0.045/hr skipped NAT. Security: SG lockdown means public IP is egress-only. Future: opt-in private-subnet-with-NAT for users who need it.

title: Phase 6b.13: Image build + ECR push in ECSProvider.deploy
description: After terraform apply creates ECR repos, rc deploy needs to build images from compose build: contexts and push them to ECR so ECS services have something to run. Today provider.deploy does emit + init + apply + output but skips image work. Demo app cloud smoke fails because task defs reference :latest tags that don't exist. Work: (a) parse compose build: stanzas during DeployContext construction; (b) in provider.deploy, after apply, for each service with a build context: authenticate to ECR (boto3 ecr.get_authorization_token), tag image with ECR URL + a content hash tag, ImageBuilder.build, ImagePusher.push; (c) update task def to reference the specific tag (not :latest) OR force-new-deployment to pull latest; (d) emit structured progress like the legacy 15-step pipeline.
acceptance_criteria: From examples/demo-app with docker running + AWS creds,  builds and pushes the api + worker images to fresh ECR repos, ECS services start successfully, ALB returns 200 on /health. Subsequent rc deploy with unchanged code is a no-op (idempotent image tag based on source hash).
notes:
PHASE 6b.13 DELIVERY — Image build + ECR push in ECSProvider.deploy

Scope
  provider.deploy(ctx) now orchestrates the full code-deploy cycle:
    emit_terraform → tf init → tf apply → build → ECR login → push →
    ecs.update_service(forceNewDeployment=True) per built service.

New module
  remote_compose/provider/ecs/ecr_auth.py
    ECRAuthenticator — callable compatible with ImagePusher's authenticator
    hook. Calls boto3 ecr.get_authorization_token, base64-decodes the token,
    pipes the password to `docker login --password-stdin`. Caches per
    registry (one login regardless of push count).

ServiceSpec additions (remote_compose/provider/base.py)
  build_context, build_args, dockerfile, image — populated from the
  docker-compose.yml at DeployContext construction time.

cli_v2 additions
  _parse_compose_services(compose_path)  loads the compose services dict
  _service_build_info(svc_compose, ...)  extracts build.context, build.args
      (handles both dict and KEY=VAL list forms), dockerfile, image
  build_deploy_context now merges the compose build info into each ServiceSpec.

Orchestration (remote_compose/provider/ecs/provider.py)
  _build_and_push_images
    - Skips services without a build context (they use pre-built images).
    - Reads ecr_repositories map from terraform outputs.
    - For each built service: ImageBuilder.build with platform=linux/amd64,
      dockerfile override if set, build_args propagated.
    - ImagePusher.push with ECRAuthenticator; one login per unique registry.
    - Warnings accumulate for missing ECR outputs / missing repos per service.
  _force_new_deployments
    - After push, ecs.update_service(forceNewDeployment=True) so running
      tasks pull the newly-pushed :latest tag.

New tests (tests/unit/test_provider_ecs/test_image_deploy.py — 6 tests)
  TestBuildPushSkippedWhenNoBuildContext
    - Services with image: only → no builds, no pushes, no forced redeploy
  TestBuildPushHappyPath
    - 2 services with build contexts → 2 builds + 2 pushes + 1 login +
      2 forceNewDeployment, correct ECR tags applied
  TestBuildPushSkipWhenNoEcrOutputs
    - Missing ecr_repositories → warning emitted, no crash
  TestECRAuthenticator
    - login succeeds and caches across calls
    - docker login failure → ECRAuthError with stderr
    - missing authorization data → ECRAuthError

Bugs discovered while writing tests
  Stacking `mock.patch("...subprocess.run")` on different import paths
  all patches the SAME subprocess.run globally — only the last patch is
  effective. Unit tests now use a single mock.patch("subprocess.run") and
  bucket calls by argv verb. Noted in inline comment.
  `shutil.which("docker")` returns the absolute path on dev boxes; test
  assertions match `cmd[0].endswith("docker")` rather than literal "docker".

Verification receipts
  pytest tests/unit/test_provider_ecs/test_image_deploy.py  → 6 passed
  pytest tests/ --ignore=tests/e2e                          → 504 passed, 4 skipped
                                                               (baseline 480/4)
  End-to-end plan smoke on the demo app:
    cd examples/demo-app && rc -c rc.yml plan
      → "provider=ecs project=demo-app
          Terraform plan: create: 53 / update: 0 / destroy: 0"

Demo cloud smoke (examples/demo-app/scripts/smoke.sh cloud) is now
UNBLOCKED. Running requires RC_E2E=1, AWS creds, docker, and ~$0.10
of compute for a 10-15 min deploy → hit → destroy cycle.
close_reason: Image build + ECR auth + push + force-new-deployment wired into provider.deploy. ECRAuthenticator handles boto3 token + docker login. 6 new unit tests. Demo plan still green (53 resources). Cloud smoke now unblocked.

title: Phase 6b.12: Wire CLI to dispatch rc.yml v2 → new Provider
description: Current state: tests/e2e invokes provider.deploy(ctx) directly; the rc CLI's deploy command still uses the legacy imperative pipeline. Demo app cloud smoke (examples/demo-app/scripts/smoke.sh cloud) therefore can't test the new provider end-to-end through the CLI. Work: (a) when rc.yml parses as v2, build a DeployContext from it and call provider.deploy/plan/destroy/etc instead of the legacy pipeline; (b) keep the legacy path alive for v1 rc.yml so start-simpli-api keeps working; (c) update the demo smoke to exercise the real CLI once wired.
acceptance_criteria: From examples/demo-app,  resolves provider=ecs, emits terraform, applies, and builds+pushes images via ImageBuilder+ImagePusher. Legacy rc.yml on the start-simpli-api repo still deploys via the imperative path. Demo cloud smoke (RC_E2E=1 ./scripts/smoke.sh cloud) passes against us-east-1.
notes:
PHASE 6b.12 DELIVERY — CLI → Provider dispatch

New module: remote_compose/cli_v2.py
  load_rc_yml(path)           → (version, raw_dict, RcConfigV2 | None)
  build_deploy_context(v2, raw, rc_yml_path) → DeployContext
    - Resolves relative compose_file against rc.yml dir

title: Stale terraform 1.1.7 install causes subprocess SIGKILL (not sandbox)
description: Originally misdiagnosed as a Claude Code sandbox issue. Reality: the Homebrew terraform formula on the dev Mac is 1.1.7 from 2022-03 (4+ years stale, x86_64 on macOS 15 with modern Gatekeeper) and macOS kills the subprocess on exec. Reproduces identically outside any sandbox — this was never a sandbox bug. Proper fix: rc doctor / rc install upgrades terraform via brew; template requires terraform >= 1.5 anyway. Flagged beads, ARCHITECTURE.md sandbox claims, and integration-test sentinel comments all need the 'sandbox' wording rewritten.
notes: Root cause: stale brew install + Gatekeeper kill on macOS. Symptoms: subprocess exit codes -9 / 137. Diagnosis trail: sysctl confirmed Intel Mac (not Apple Silicon / Rosetta), terraform binary linked to Cellar/terraform/1.1.7, user confirmed it's an old Intel box. Action: rc-e5u.21 (rc doctor) handles this generically. In-session work that I claimed was 'blocked by sandbox' can actually run on this box once terraform is upgraded.
close_reason: Resolved by rc-e5u.21 (rc doctor / rc install). The root cause was stale brew install, not a sandbox — rc doctor --fix now upgrades terraform via the platform package manager. Not a live issue.

title: Phase 5: Architecture — module layout, deprecation plan for imperative services
description: Lock the module layout before implementation starts. Decide where the Provider interface lives, where each provider's code + terraform templates live, how rc.yml v2 parsing/migration is organized, how the CLI dispatches to providers, and how the existing imperative services (aws_service, ecs_service, efs_service, etc.) are deprecated incrementally rather than deleted. Also settle how terraform is invoked (subprocess vs python-terraform library) and how terraform state is passed to the CLI for status/logs queries.
acceptance_criteria: Module tree is drawn with file paths. Each existing imperative service has a planned fate (keep, replace, delete, wrap). Terraform invocation approach is chosen. CLI dispatch mechanism is specified.
notes:
PHASE 5 ARCHITECTURE

Module layout, import rules, and imperative-service deprecation plan are fully
specified in the Phase 2 notes (rc-e5u.2). This phase adds the three
architectural pieces not covered there:

==============================================================
1. CLI DISPATCH MECHANISM
==============================================================

- Existing cli.py (Click-based) stays as the entry point; no rewrite.
- Each top-level command (deploy / plan / status / logs / exec / rollback /
  destroy / redeploy / migrate) resolves a Provider instance once:
      provider = remote_compose.provider.get(rc_yml.provider)()
  Then delegates:
      provider.deploy(ctx)  # or plan/status/... depending on command
- --provider <name> flag overrides rc.yml for one-off testing.
- Provider is resolved via the registry populated at import time by
  remote_compose.provider.{fake,ecs,k8s}.
- Every provider module self-registers: its __init__ calls
  remote_compose.provider.register(name, cls).

==============================================================
2. ERROR HANDLING
==============================================================

- All provider-surfaced exceptions derive from ProviderError
  (see remote_compose/provider/base.py).
- CLI top-level catches ProviderError, prints the sanitized message to stderr,
  exits non-zero. Existing log_sanitizer is reused.
- --verbose flag promotes to traceback printing.
- Unexpected (non-ProviderError) exceptions always print traceback — those
  are bugs, not user errors.

==============================================================
3. PROGRESS REPORTING  (NFR-5)
==============================================================

- Current 15-step pipeline output (`[N/M] StepName... done (Xs)`) is the UX
  baseline.
- Introduce a ProgressReporter protocol:
      class ProgressReporter(Protocol):
          def step(self, idx: int, total: int, name: str) -> "StepCtx": ...
          class StepCtx:
              def done(self, duration_s: float, warnings: list[str]): ...
              def fail(self, err: Exception): ...
- Providers accept a ProgressReporter in their constructor (default =
  TtyProgressReporter). Tests inject a RecordingProgressReporter to assert
  on the step sequence without touching stdout.
- This replaces the deployment_pipeline step abstraction but preserves its
  user-visible output.

==============================================================
REMAINING ARCHITECTURAL ITEMS — DEFERRED
==============================================================

- Concurrency model for Provider.deploy (ServiceSpec parallelism). Default
  sequential at first; revisit when a real deployment motivates it.
- Pluggable terraform-runner backends (subprocess vs library). Locked to
  subprocess per Phase 2; no change here.
- Output format for machine-readable CLI (--json). Nice to have, not in v1
  scope.
close_reason: Module layout + deprecation plan recorded in rc-e5u.2; this phase adds CLI dispatch, error handling, and ProgressReporter protocol. Deferred items (deploy concurrency, --json output) noted.

title: _sync_alb_to_db and teardown_vpc use factory without region/credential
description: alb_service.py:426 _sync_alb_to_db creates client without region/credential context. vpc_service.py:365 teardown_vpc same issue. If resources in non-default region, teardown/sync will fail silently. Fix: accept and pass region/credential parameters.

title: VPC _get_vpc_cidr returns fallback 10.0.0.0/8 instead of failing
description: efs_service.py:1146 returns '10.0.0.0/8' when VPC has no CidrBlock. A /8 CIDR creates overly permissive NFS security group rules. Should raise error instead of silently defaulting. Fix: raise EFSError if no CidrBlock found.

title: logs:CreateLogGroup IAM policy grants Resource: * — overly broad
description: ecs_service.py:1006-1017 inline policy for CreateLogGroup uses Resource: '*'. Should be scoped to specific log group pattern like arn:aws:logs:*:*:log-group:/ecs/*. Unnecessary broad permissions.

title: Exception chains missing 'from e' throughout codebase
description: ecs_deployment_service.py:292 and many other locations raise new exceptions without 'from e', destroying original tracebacks. E.g., raise ECSDeploymentError(f'Deployment failed: {e}') loses root cause. Fix: use 'raise XError(...) from e' pattern throughout.

title: requiresCompatibilities defaults to empty list, fallback to FARGATE never reached
description: ecs.py model field defaults to list (empty []). to_aws_format() checks 'is not None' which is always True for [], so empty list sent to AWS instead of ['FARGATE']. AWS requires at least one. Fix: change default to ['FARGATE'] or fix conditional to truthy check.

title: DockerContext.save() race condition + ECSService.clean() never called
description: 1) contexts.py:57-61 save() clears other defaults then saves, not atomic. Two concurrent saves with is_default=True can both succeed. Fix: use select_for_update or transaction.atomic. 2) ecs.py:496-505 clean() validates min/max/desired counts but never called by save() or objects.create(). Fix: override save() to call full_clean() or add DB constraint.

title: Deployment model requires context FK but ECS deployments don't use DockerContext
description: deployments.py:29-33 has non-nullable context FK to DockerContext. ECS deployments have no DockerContext, forcing _create_deployment_record to leave deployment unsaved (deployment.id=None). Later steps check .id, skip status updates. Fix: make context nullable or create ECS deployment tracking path.

title: TOCTOU race in _get_or_create_service_model
description: ecs.py:168-216 checks DB then checks AWS then creates record. Between check and create, another process could create same record. No get_or_create or unique constraint. Fix: use ECSServiceModel.objects.get_or_create() or wrap in select_for_update() transaction.

title: convert() saves model but convert_preprocessed()/convert_per_service() don't
description: compose_converter.py convert() at line 131 calls task_definition.save(). convert_preprocessed() and convert_per_service() return unsaved models. Inconsistent side effects. Callers of convert() get unexpected DB write, callers of others can forget to save. Fix: make all three consistent — either always save or never save.

title: Inconsistent deployment status: string literals vs enum members
description: initialization.py:78 uses 'failed', multi_service.py:600 uses 'completed' as raw strings. finalization.py:36 uses Deployment.DeploymentStatus.COMPLETED. If enum values change, string literals silently break. Fix: always use enum constants for status assignments.

title: FARGATE_INCOMPATIBLE_FEATURES dict unused + _resolve_yaml_anchors is no-op
description: 1) compose_preprocessor.py:153-164 defines FARGATE_INCOMPATIBLE_FEATURES but _detect_incompatibilities doesn't use it, uses inline checks instead. 2) _resolve_yaml_anchors (preprocessor.py:375-402) does yaml.safe_load then yaml.dump then caller does yaml.safe_load again — redundant. Fix: use dict in detection or delete it. Return parsed dict directly from _resolve_yaml_anchors.

title: STS session token not supported in credential handling
description: All credential paths (aws_client_factory.py:158-167, ecs_service.py:62-68, etc) only pass access_key_id and secret_access_key. If stored credential has session_token from STS AssumeRole, it's silently dropped. boto3.client() needs aws_session_token parameter. Fix: pass session_token through all credential paths.

title: ecs_service.py (1045 lines) and efs_service.py (1327 lines) need splitting
description: ecs_service.py handles cluster mgmt, task defs, services, tasks, network discovery, IAM roles. Network discovery duplicates VPCService, IAM is its own concern. efs_service.py has file systems, access points, mount targets, security groups (duplicates SecurityGroupService), and ECS volume helpers. Fix: extract IAM to helper, delegate VPC/SG to existing services, split EFS into focused modules.

title: ALB/target group name truncation causes collisions
description: alb_service.py:70-71, 113-114, 260-261 naively truncate names to 32 chars. 'my-very-long-cluster-name-alpha-alb' and 'my-very-long-cluster-name-bravo-alb' both truncate identically. Fix: append short SHA256 hash suffix to preserve uniqueness when truncating.

title: _bootstrap_django does 7 things — split into focused functions
description: cli.py:89-171 handles AWS profile setup, Django settings config, secret key generation/persistence, encryption key lookup, django.setup(), schema version checking, and database migration. 7 distinct responsibilities. Fix: break into _set_aws_profile, _get_or_create_secret_key, _configure_django_settings, _migrate_if_needed.

title: CLI resource leaks: backup_file no-op, temp file leak, fd leak
description: 1) cli.py:1202-1203 has no-op ternary: both branches identical (backup_file if '/' in backup_file else backup_file). 2) _write_service_config temp file leaked on exception, not cleaned up in finally. 3) _exec_interactive leaks /dev/tty fd if subprocess.run raises (cli.py:353-358). Fix: fix ternary, use context manager for temp file and tty.

title: Dead code and duplication in CLI event handling
description: _step_counter (cli.py:243-262) is dead code, never used. provision and deploy both define near-identical handler lambdas for pipeline events (lines 548-561 vs 684-703). Same pattern duplicated in management commands ecs_provision.py:108-123 and ecs_deploy_compose.py:139-163. Fix: delete _step_counter, extract _make_pipeline_handler() factory.

title: _parse_memory unit parsing wrong for bare numbers
description: compose_converter.py:697-707 defaults bare integers to megabytes but Docker Compose treats bare numbers as bytes. 536870912 (512MB in bytes) parsed as 536870912 MB. Regex also doesn't handle mb/gb/mi/gi suffixes. Fix: bare numbers should be bytes, add mb/gb support, align with Docker memory parsing.

title: Hardcoded values scattered: regions, timeouts, ports, health paths, IAM roles

IAM role 'ecsTaskExecutionRole' 6 times. DB port 5432, cache port 6379. Presigned URL ExpiresIn=7200. ALB SSL policy. Fix: define constants, pull from REMOTE_COMPOSE settings dict.

title: S3: Add database engine abstraction to db backup/restore
description: cli.py:1012-1042, 1162-1218 — Currently hardcoded to pg_dump/pg_restore. Add rc.yml config field 'backup.engine' (default: 'postgresql'). Create abstract BackupEngine class with PostgresBackupEngine implementation. Support future engines (mysql, sqlite) via the abstraction. At minimum, document that only PostgreSQL is currently supported.

title: S3: Fix ALB name truncation to use hash suffix; replace print() with logging in ECSDeploymentService
description: alb_service.py:69-70, 112-113, 259-260 — When name exceeds 32 chars, use name[:24]-{hash[:7]} pattern instead of blind truncation. ecs_deployment_service.py:916-921 — Replace print() calls in _log_step with self.log_info()/log_warning(). Also fix monkey-patched deployment._duration (lines 242,270) — return duration as separate value or store in deployment.metadata.

title: S3: Add schema version check to CLI bootstrap; persist and generate SECRET_KEY per-project

Only run migrate when version changes or on first run. cli.py:138 — Generate a random SECRET_KEY on first run and persist to ~/.remote-compose/<project>/secret_key. Load from disk on subsequent runs.

title: S3: Move EFS security group logic to SecurityGroupService
description: efs_service.py:1018-1128 — get_or_create_efs_security_group(), _get_vpc_cidr(), authorize_security_group_for_efs() should live in SecurityGroupService. Also fix: recursive call with no depth limit on duplicate group (1125-1127, add max retries), and _get_vpc_cidr fallback to 10.0.0.0/8 (line 1146, should raise error not fall back). Also fix _find_file_system_by_name N+1 API calls (231-255, use tags from describe_file_systems response).

title: S3: Split PipelineContext into typed sub-contexts
description:
context.py:27-240 — PipelineContext has 50+ fields. Split into:
1. DeploymentConfig (compose_file, project_name, cluster_name, region, domain, etc.)
2. InfrastructureState (vpc_id, subnet_ids, security_group_ids, alb_arn, etc.)
3. ImageState (ecr_repos, built_images, image_tags, etc.)

title: S3: Consolidate volume conversion and unify _sanitize_name
description:
compose_converter.py:
1. Merge _convert_volumes (lines 892-1000) and _convert_volumes_with_efs (lines 1001-1081) into one method with optional efs_config parameter. HOST_PATH and BIND handling is identical copy-paste.
2. Unify _sanitize_name: converter version (line 1252, preserves case, 255 chars) vs preprocessor version (line 993, lowercase, 128 chars). Pick one behavior — lowercase + 128 chars is safer for ECR repos. Move to shared utils.

title: S3: Remove DB side effects from compose converter
description: compose_converter.py:306,489 — convert_preprocessed() and convert_per_service() call task_definition.save(). A converter should transform data, not persist it. Move .save() calls to the pipeline step or service layer that calls the converter. This enables dry-run mode and makes the converter testable without a database.

title: S3: Extract shared conversion core from 3 convert methods
description: compose_converter.py:62-501 — convert(), convert_preprocessed(), and convert_per_service() repeat: validate→iterate→convert→calc resources→hash→query existing→build→save. title: S3: Create shared poll_until() utility and migrate all 8 wait methods
description:
Create remote_compose/utils/polling.py with:
  def poll_until(check_fn, timeout, interval=10, timeout_msg='Operation timed out', logger=None):
      start = time.time(); while time.time() - start < timeout: if check_fn(): return True; time.sleep(interval); raise TimeoutError(timeout_msg)

Migrate these 8 methods:
- ecs_service.py:679-732 (wait_for_service_stable)
- efs_service.py:405-441, 868-931, 933-970 (3 wait methods)
- vpc_service.py:333-367, 482-505 (NAT gateway)
- alb_service.py:724-755 (ALB active)
- service_connect_service.py:230-286 (wait_for_operation)
Each becomes a ~5 line wrapper around poll_until(). Cuts ~200 lines total.
close_reason: Shared poll_until() utility created, 8 wait methods migrated. -186 lines net

title: S3: Extract _get_cluster() and _resolve_service() CLI helpers

Sprint 3 tackles all the copy-paste duplication and god objects. Extract shared utilities, consolidate duplicate conversion logic, decompose the CLI monolith, and split the pipeline context.

Includes: ico, 26s, vfv, 81v, snq, xjl, v94, 0fs

title: ALB name truncation causes collisions; ECSDeploymentService._log_step uses print()
description:
alb_service.py:69-70, 112-113, 259-260 - Blind truncation to 32 chars means 'my-very-long-cluster-name-production' and 'my-very-long-cluster-name-staging' collide. Use hash suffix for uniqueness.

title: CLI bootstrap runs migrations on every invocation + hardcoded SECRET_KEY
description:
cli.py:144 - call_command('migrate', '--run-syncdb', verbosity=0) runs on every CLI command including read-only ones like 'rc status'. Adds noticeable latency. Should only run on first setup or version mismatch.

cli.py:138 - SECRET_KEY='rc-cli-key' is static for every installation. If the API is ever served from this bootstrap, every installation shares the same signing key. Should be generated and persisted per-project.

title: EFS service mixes concerns — manages security groups internally instead of using SecurityGroupService
description: efs_service.py:1018-1128 - get_or_create_efs_security_group(), _get_vpc_cidr(), authorize_security_group_for_efs() are EC2 security group operations embedded in an EFS service. SecurityGroupService already exists for this. Also: recursive call with no depth limit on duplicate group (line 1125-1127) and _get_vpc_cidr falls back to 10.0.0.0/8 which opens NFS to entire class A range (line 1146). Additionally _find_file_system_by_name makes N+1 describe_tags calls when tags are already in describe_file_systems response.

title: db backup/restore hardcoded to PostgreSQL with no abstraction
description: cli.py:1012-1042, 1162-1218 - db backup and db restore generate shell scripts hardcoding pg_dump, pg_restore, PGPASSWORD, POSTGRES_HOST, POSTGRES_USER, POSTGRES_DB. No database type abstraction. If this tool is meant to be generic, need pluggable engine support or clear documentation that only PostgreSQL is supported with a backup.engine config field.

title: PipelineContext is a 50+ field god object — split into sub-contexts
description: deployment_pipeline/context.py:27-240 - PipelineContext holds everything from VPC CIDRs to cert ARNs to EFS configs to Django settings. Impossible to know which fields a step reads/writes, creates implicit coupling, will grow unboundedly. Split into sub-contexts: InfrastructureState, ImageState, DeploymentConfig, etc.
close_reason: Context god object decomposed

title: Compose converter: 3 nearly identical convert methods + duplicated volume conversion
description:
compose_converter.py:62-501 - convert(), convert_preprocessed(), and convert_per_service() repeat the same pattern: validate inputs, iterate services, convert, calculate Fargate resources, compute hash, query existing task defs, build ECSTaskDefinition, save. Also:
- _convert_volumes and _convert_volumes_with_efs duplicate most logic (lines 892-1081)
- Duplicate _sanitize_name with different behavior between converter (preserves case, 255 chars) and preprocessor (lowercase, 128 chars) — will cause ECR repo names to not match task def container names
- Duplicate build-key computation in 3 places (build.py:43, multi_service.py:189-192,238, converter:388)
- converter calls task_definition.save() — converter should not have DB side effects (breaks dry-run/testing)
Extract shared helpers, remove DB side effects from converter, consolidate volume conversion.

title: Duplicated polling/wait loops across 8+ services — need shared poll_until()

Identical timeout-polling pattern (start_time, while loop, try/except, time.sleep, raise on timeout) appears in:

title: CLI monolith: massive duplication of cluster lookup, service resolution, progress handlers
description:
cli.py has systematic copy-paste:
- Cluster lookup pattern repeated 8 times (lines 264,504,617,683,773,857,916,1329)
- Service name resolution repeated 5 times (lines 271-279, 691-697, 782-789, etc.)
- Event handler callback duplicated between provision and deploy (lines 424-434 vs 561-576)

title: copilot.8: addons CFN templates — detect, list, document not-yet-handled
description: copilot/<svc>/addons/*.yml define extra CFN resources (RDS instances, S3 buckets, DynamoDB, etc.). Out of scope for first cut. Detect their presence and emit a clear human-readable summary at the end of import: 'Found 3 addon templates; manual translation required: <list>'. Each addon type gets a stub bead the user can pick up (RDS → 'set up your own RDS, point DATABASE_URL at it'; S3 → 'use rc.yml backup.bucket OR add to terraform/'). Test asserts the summary is emitted with a fixture containing addons.

title: autoimport.5: P3 backlog — celerybrowser/eval-app/docs prod Dockerfiles + non-standard port mappings
description: celerybrowser exposes 7788/5901-5903/9222 (VNC + chrome remote debug); ECS task net mode SG rules need to handle these. eval-app + docs only have local Dockerfiles; need prod Dockerfile. These are sentinal-side changes, not portable-deploy provider changes. Document as a follow-up the sentinal team can pick up.
close_reason: P3 backlog — these are SENTINAL-side changes (Dockerfiles, port mappings) not rc provider changes. Tracked for the sentinal team, not blocking rc. The auto-import path itself doesn't need them: cli_v2.build_deploy_context honors compose.exclude/include cleanly.

title: multidomain.6: P3 backlog — celerybrowser, eval-app, docs production Dockerfiles
description: Followups not blocking the core multi-domain feature. (a) celerybrowser needs ports 7788/5901-5903/9222 — non-standard port mapping; investigate ECS task net mode SG rules. (b) eval-app: production-ready Dockerfile + decide what subdomain. (c) docs: only has compose/local/docs/Dockerfile target=dev; needs a prod Dockerfile build target.

title: Gap: _zone_from_domain's 2-label heuristic is wrong for nested subdomains
description: Provider's _zone_from_domain('migration-test.api.startsimpli.com') returns 'startsimpli.com' — assumes the R53 zone is always the apex. Real accounts often delegate subdomain zones (e.g. api.startsimpli.com), leaving the parent undelegated. The data.aws_route53_zone lookup then fails at apply. Fix (landed): provider_config.ecs.route53_zone explicit override bypasses the heuristic. Smarter future fix: list zones via boto3 at emit time and pick the longest-suffix match of the target domain.

title: Gap: all secrets attach to every service (no per-service scope)
description: Provider currently does 'for svc_view in services_view: svc_view[secrets] = secrets_view' so every service task def gets ALL secret entries — e.g. postgres container receives DJANGO_SUPERUSER_PASSWORD + SECRET_KEY + REDIS_URL etc. that it has no use for. Correctness is fine but wastes env-var slots (ECS caps 100/container) and leaks unnecessary values to workloads that shouldn't see them. Fix: allow rc.yml v2 secrets to optionally scope to a list of service names, defaulting to all if unspecified.

title: Gap: rc destroy leaves orphan container-insights log group
description: ECS auto-creates /aws/ecs/containerinsights/<cluster>/performance when Container Insights is enabled. Terraform doesn't manage it, so 'rc destroy' cleanly removes everything else but leaves this log group behind. Fix: either import/manage it as an aws_cloudwatch_log_group resource in cluster.tf.j2, or add a post-destroy cleanup hook. Found during Mini v0 cleanup verification.

title: Gap: aws_service_discovery_service.failure_threshold deprecation
description: terraform validate emits 7 deprecation warnings — 'failure_threshold = 1' is no longer supported by AWS and will be removed in a future terraform-aws-provider major version. Template: remote_compose/provider/ecs/templates/service_discovery.tf.j2. Fix: drop the failure_threshold line from health_check_config {}. Non-blocking for Mini v0 but will break on provider major bump.

title: Phase 6b.16: Postgres-on-EFS access point uid mismatch
description: EFS access points enforce posix_user=1000:1000 (per our template). postgres:16-alpine container runs initdb which tries chown on the data directory; fails with 'Operation not permitted' because the container user (postgres, typically uid 999 or 70) can't change ownership on a 1000:1000 mount. Fix options: (a) parameterize access point posix_user per service via rc.yml; (b) drop access points for EFS and use raw mount with iam auth; (c) ship a postgres base image that matches uid 1000. For now demo works around by not using EFS for the db service; production guidance should recommend RDS for postgres instead of ECS-on-EFS.
acceptance_criteria: A demo or integration test deploys an ECS+EFS postgres service and initdb completes. Access point uid is either documented as parameterizable or replaced with a mount strategy that lets postgres chown.
close_reason: EFS volumes now support per-service uid/gid/mode on access points (default 1000/1000/0755). postgres:16-alpine uid=70 wired and verified. Separately landed 'stateful' detection: any service with EFS volumes gets deployment_minimum_healthy_percent=0/maximum_percent=100 so the replacement task waits for the primary to stop before mounting — caught while Mini v3 smoke corrupted postgres data under rolling deploy. End-to-end proof: Mini v3 deploy → migrate → superuser → admin login 302 → force postgres restart → admin login 302 again with the same credentials persisted in EFS. 6 new tests, suite 537 passed / 4 skipped.

title: Phase 6b.5: ECS provider — custom domain + ACM + Route 53
description: When rc.yml v2 domain is set, provision ACM certificate (DNS-validated via Route 53), wire ALB 443 listener + redirect from 80, create A-record alias to ALB.

title: Phase 6b.4: ECS provider — secrets integration (file + aws_sm)
description: Route rc.yml v2 secrets through ECS task definitions without leaking values. File-source secrets materialize as aws_secretsmanager_secret + aws_secretsmanager_secret_version + task definition secrets[] block. aws_sm-source secrets reference existing ARNs.
acceptance_criteria: Secret values never appear in emitted HCL or in terraform state plaintext (verified by sentinel test); task definitions have correct secrets[] with valueFrom pointing at the right ARN.
notes:
PHASE 6b.4 DELIVERY — Secrets integration (file + aws_sm)

Contract
  source: file  — terraform creates an empty aws_secretsmanager_secret with
                  a placeholder secret_version. lifecycle.ignore_changes =
                  [secret_string] so subsequent applies don't overwrite the
                  real value uploaded by `rc secrets push` (legacy command,
                  unchanged). Secret ARN is referenced by task definitions
                  and the task execution IAM policy.
  source: aws_sm — no terraform resource created. Existing ARN is referenced
                   directly in task defs + IAM policy.
  source: k8s_secret / gcp_sm — silently skipped on the ECS provider. Other
                                 providers consume these.
  Unknown source → ProviderConfigError with the bad source name.

Env var naming
  Default: secret.name sanitized → uppercase (django → DJANGO,
           my-db-password → MY_DB_PASSWORD). Explicit override (env_name
           field) is a future extension.

Hard invariant
  Secret VALUES never appear in terraform HCL or terraform state. Enforced
  by contract-suite sentinel test plus a provider-level sentinel test
  (test_sentinel_never_appears_in_any_hcl).

New / updated files
  remote_compose/provider/ecs/templates/secrets.tf.j2  — NEW, renders only
    when has_file_secrets. Placeholder + ignore_changes.
  remote_compose/provider/ecs/templates/iam.tf.j2      — UPDATED, conditional
    task_execution_secrets policy listing every referenced secret ARN.
  remote_compose/provider/ecs/templates/services.tf.j2 — UPDATED, conditional
    containerDefinitions.secrets[] with name + valueFrom per secret.
  remote_compose/provider/ecs/provider.py              — UPDATED, builds
    file_secrets / aws_sm_secrets / secrets_view / all_secret_arns context;
    _env_name_for_secret helper added.
  tests/unit/test_provider_ecs/test_secrets.py         — NEW, 16 tests.

Verification receipts
  pytest tests/unit/test_provider_ecs/test_secrets.py
    → 16 passed in 0.80s
  pytest tests/
    → 424 passed, 9 skipped in 7.48s  (baseline 408/9)
  ⚠️ Real AWS secret read-after-apply: still sandbox-blocked.
close_reason: Secrets integration done. file-source creates placeholder aws_secretsmanager_secret with ignore_changes lifecycle (value uploaded by rc secrets push). aws_sm-source references existing ARN. Task def containerDefinitions.secrets[] + IAM policy both wired. Sentinel confirms values never enter HCL. 16 new tests pass; 424 total.

title: AWSClientFactory singleton not safe for multi-tenant Django; 12 convenience methods add no value

aws_client_factory.py:188-274 - 12 convenience methods (get_ecs_client, get_ecr_client, etc.) are all single-line wrappers around get_client(). 90 lines of code with zero additional logic. Callers can just use factory.get_client('ecs', ...).

value: Mini v3 stateful EFS runbook: (1) rc.yml volumes entry gains optional uid/gid/mode (default 1000/1000/0755). postgres:16-alpine = 70, postgres (debian) = 999, redis:7-alpine = 999, mysql = 999. Mode 0700 for db dirs. (2) Provider auto-sets deployment_minimum_healthy_percent=0/maximum=100 on ANY service with EFS mounts — rolling deploys corrupt stateful EFS when two tasks briefly mount the same dir. (3) postgres-on-EFS baseline throughput is slow: 50KB/s per GiB stored, ~100 MiB/s burst initially. Big restores can take hours. (4) aws ecs execute-command swallows stdout from complex scripts in non-TTY mode — base64+heredoc+pipe scripts run correctly but return empty output. Use side-effect tests (curl ALB) for reality-check.

Mini v0 runbook (ss migration us-west-1 smoke): 1) rc.yml tailored with project=rc-test-*, region=us-west-1, vpc_cidr=10.42.0.0/16, aws_profile=debuggai. 2) Stub docker-compose.yml with public images (busybox:latest for app/workers, postgres:16-alpine, redis:7-alpine, nginx:alpine). 3) For Mini v0 specifically: skip postgres volumes (hits rc-e5u.27 EFS chown bug) and set nginx health_check_path: / (stock nginx:alpine 404s on /health). 4) rc deploy fresh ~200s, redeploy ~70s. 5) Post-destroy verify needs manual cleanup of /aws/ecs/containerinsights/<cluster>/performance log group (provider gap, filed). 6) Verification sweep: ecs clusters, VPCs tagged Project, ALBs, target groups, EFS, ECR, servicediscovery namespaces, log groups, IAM roles starting rc-test-, secrets, security groups by tag.

Mini v2 secrets workflow (v2 rc.yml + per-key SM): (1) declare secrets with source=file+path in rc.yml; (2) rc deploy creates SM placeholders + task defs referencing arn:KEY:: per key; (3) tasks will fail health until secrets are real — this is expected; (4) rc secrets push parses each .env file, puts SecretString=json.dumps({KEY:value}), force-rolls services; (5) tasks boot with env vars from SM. Caveat: django entrypoint does NOT run migrations — 'aws ecs execute-command django -- python manage.py migrate --noinput' is a required post-secrets step, else admin hits 'relation django_site does not exist'. createsuperuser --noinput honors DJANGO_SUPERUSER_{EMAIL,PASSWORD} when USERNAME_FIELD='email' on User model. Every task def currently gets ALL secrets across ALL services — tracked as follow-up bead for per-service scoping.

rc-only acceptance for start-simpli green 2026-04-26: single 'rc up --from-compose docker-compose.local.yml --aws-profile default --region us-west-1 --ttl 4h' deploys django+nginx+postgres+redis+celery-worker+celery-beat to healthy on us-west-1, ALB serves 200 with celery: healthy. Test script scripts/test-startsimpli-end-to-end.sh runs 7-step acceptance (destroy, up, poll-healthy, curl, verify celery, destroy, registry-empty). Critical defaults that make this work: ALB matcher 200-499 (404 from / is ok), auto-EFS for compose named-volumes on singletons (celery-beat), nginx auto-fix to ECS-aware conf with Cloud Map FQDN + resolver, terraform import on orphan container-insights log group via static local.public_subnet_count, rc destroy unregisters ephemeral entry, scaffolder injects DJANGO_ALLOWED_HOSTS=* for rc-test-* projects via framework registry. Verified end-to-end against real AWS, 5 e2e runs total — final clean PASS.

start-simpli admin login requires EMAIL in the 'Email address' form field (USERNAME_FIELD='email' in apps/users/models.py). Django createsuperuser --noinput honors DJANGO_SUPERUSER_EMAIL + _PASSWORD; the _USERNAME env is ignored when USERNAME_FIELD is not 'username'. Custom csrf_failure handler at apps/authentication/views.csrf_failure returns JSON {error:CSRF_VALIDATION_FAILED}, easy to mistake for a real CSRF issue vs stale cookies. ALB target group gets new DNS name on each cold stack (e.g. alb-1509417821) so CSRF_TRUSTED_ORIGINS env must be updated + redeployed after first deploy, or use ALLOWED_HOSTS='*' + skip CSRF_TRUSTED_ORIGINS for test stacks.
